attributes.name: activity_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or description of the underwriting activity performed. Provides business-friendly label for the activity type.

attributes.name: activity_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments recorded by the underwriter or system regarding this activity. Provides additional context, rationale, or instructions related to the workflow event.

attributes.name: activity_status
attributes.description: Current status of the activity within the workflow. Indicates whether the activity has been completed, is pending, in progress, failed, or was cancelled.

attributes.name: activity_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the underwriting activity occurred or was recorded in the system. Primary business event timestamp for workflow tracking and Service Level Agreement (SLA) monitoring.

attributes.name: activity_type_code
attributes.description: Code representing the type of underwriting workflow activity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EVIDENCE_ORDERED|EVIDENCE_RECEIVED|CASE_ASSIGNED|CASE_REASSIGNED|PRIORITY_CHANGED|REFERRAL_SENIOR_UW|REINSURANCE_SUBMITTED|DECISION_RENDERED|COUNTER_OFFER_ISSUED|APPLICANT_NOTIFICATION_SENT|SLA_ESCALATION_TRIGGERED|QUEUE_ENTRY|QUEUE_EXIT|MEDICAL_REVIEW_REQUESTED|FINANCIAL_REVIEW_REQUESTED|APS_ORDERED|MIB_LOOKUP_COMPLETED|CASE_SUSPENDED|CASE_REOPENED|CASE_WITHDRAWN|REQUIREMENTS_WAIVED — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: assigned_underwriter_name
attributes.description: Full name of the underwriter assigned to the case at the time of this activity. Provides human-readable identification for reporting and workload distribution analysis.

attributes.name: automated_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether the activity was performed by an automated system or rules engine versus a human underwriter. True for automated activities, False for manual activities.

attributes.name: case_priority_level
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the case at the time of this activity. Determines processing urgency and Service Level Agreement (SLA) targets. May change throughout case lifecycle.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this activity record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: decision_rationale
attributes.description: Explanation or justification for the underwriting decision rendered in this activity. Provides business rationale for approval, decline, or counter-offer decisions.

attributes.name: duration_seconds
attributes.description: Duration of the activity in seconds. Measures the time spent on manual activities or the elapsed time for system processes. Used for productivity and efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: escalation_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the reason for escalation or referral to senior underwriter. Examples include high Net Amount at Risk (NAR), complex medical history, Stranger-Originated Life Insurance (STOLI) suspicion, Anti-Money Laundering (AML) concern.

attributes.name: evidence_type_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the type of evidence ordered or received in this activity. Examples include Attending Physician Statement (APS), Medical Information Bureau (MIB) report, financial statements, paramedical exam. Populated for evidence-related activities.

attributes.name: evidence_vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-party vendor or service provider from whom evidence was ordered or received. Examples include Medical Information Bureau (MIB), paramedical exam providers, Attending Physician Statement (APS) retrieval services.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this activity record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: Status of the case immediately after this activity occurred. Captures state transition for audit trail and workflow analysis.

attributes.name: notification_channel
attributes.description: Communication channel used to send notification to applicant or agent. Values include email, postal mail, phone, customer portal, or fax.

attributes.name: notification_type_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the type of notification sent to the applicant or agent. Examples include decision letter, requirements letter, counter-offer notification, decline notification. Populated for applicant notification activities.

attributes.name: performing_system_name
attributes.description: Name of the system or automated process that performed the activity when not initiated by a human user. Examples include automated rules engine, batch process, or integration service.

attributes.name: performing_user_name
attributes.description: Full name of the user who performed the activity. Provides human-readable identification for audit and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: previous_priority_level
attributes.description: Priority level of the case before this activity. Relevant for priority change activities to track escalations and de-escalations.

attributes.name: previous_status
attributes.description: Status of the case immediately before this activity occurred. Captures state transition for audit trail and workflow analysis.

attributes.name: queue_entry_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the case entered the queue associated with this activity. Used to calculate queue residence time and Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance.

attributes.name: queue_exit_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the case exited the queue associated with this activity. Used to calculate queue residence time and throughput metrics.

attributes.name: queue_name
attributes.description: Name of the work queue where the case resided at the time of this activity. Examples include New Business (NB) Intake Queue, Medical Review Queue, Senior Underwriter Queue, Reinsurance Submission Queue.

attributes.name: reinsurance_submission_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether this activity involved submission to a reinsurer for facultative or automatic reinsurance placement. True if reinsurance was submitted, False otherwise.

attributes.name: reinsurer_name
attributes.description: Name of the reinsurance company to which the case was submitted. Populated for reinsurance submission activities.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of whether this activity resulted in a Service Level Agreement (SLA) breach. True if the activity was completed after the SLA due timestamp, False otherwise.

attributes.name: sla_due_timestamp
attributes.description: Target date and time by which the activity or case processing step must be completed to meet Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitments. Used for escalation triggers and performance monitoring.

attributes.name: source_system_name
attributes.description: Name of the source system that generated this activity record. Examples include Underwriting Workbench, Policy Administration System, automated rules engine.

attributes.name: underwriting_team_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the underwriting team responsible for the case at the time of this activity. Used for team-level workload and performance reporting.

attributes.name: underwriting_team_name
attributes.description: Name of the underwriting team responsible for the case. Examples include Medical Underwriting Team, Financial Underwriting Team, Senior Underwriting Team.

products.name: counter_offer
products.description: Underwriting counter-offer record issued when an application cannot be approved as applied but can be approved under modified terms. Captures original applied-for coverage amount and risk class, counter-offer terms (modified face amount, table rating, flat extra, exclusion rider, product change), counter-offer issue date, applicant response deadline, and applicant acceptance or rejection status. Manages the counter-offer negotiation workflow between underwriting and the applicant/agent.
products.reference: NAIC Adverse Action Notice Requirements; State DOI Regulations

attributes.name: counter_offer_id
attributes.description: Primary key for counter_offer

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the new business application that triggered this counter-offer. Links to the underwriting application record.

attributes.name: communication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to correspondence.communication. Business justification: Counter-offers are formal communications requiring applicant acceptance/rejection. Core business process: modified offer presentation and response tracking. Regulatory requirement: clear disclosure of

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underwriter who issued this counter-offer. Links to the employee or underwriter resource record.

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policy.in_force_policy. Business justification: Counter offers issued during underwriting must reference the issued policy to track acceptance outcomes, link counter offer terms to final policy terms, and support regulatory reporting on counter off

attributes.name: insurance_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Counter offers generate formal offer documents with modified terms sent to applicants. Business process: acceptance/rejection tracking and signature collection require linking counter offers to their

attributes.name: mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.mortality_table. Business justification: Counter offers document mortality table basis for modified risk class pricing and repricing justification. Real business need: repricing calculations, customer communication support, policy issue vali

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: The modified product code offered by underwriting if a product change is recommended (e.g., offering Term instead of Whole Life (WL) due to insurability concerns).

attributes.name: premium_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.premium_schedule. Business justification: Counter offers with modified risk class, table ratings, or face amount require new premium schedule calculation. Business process: counter offer acceptance by applicant triggers billing setup with rev

attributes.name: primary_counter_applied_risk_class_id
attributes.description: Reference to the risk class originally applied for by the applicant (e.g., Preferred Plus, Standard Non-Smoker).

attributes.name: producer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the writing agent or producer who submitted the original application and will communicate the counter-offer to the applicant.

attributes.name: uw_decision_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to underwriting.decision. Business justification: Counter offers are issued based on formal underwriting decisions. When an application cannot be approved as applied, a counter offer is generated referencing the decision that triggered it. Removing u

attributes.name: acceptance_method
attributes.description: The method by which the applicant accepted the counter-offer (e.g., wet signature on paper form, electronic signature via portal, recorded verbal acceptance, agent attestation).
attributes.references: ESIGN Act and UETA Electronic Signature Standards

attributes.name: acceptance_signature_date
attributes.description: The date the applicant signed the acceptance of the counter-offer terms. Used to establish the effective date of coverage under modified terms.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation on Policy Delivery

attributes.name: annual_premium_equivalent
attributes.description: The annualized premium amount for the counter-offer, calculated as 10% of single premium or 100% of regular premium. Used for new business (NB) production reporting and commission calculations.

attributes.name: applied_face_amount
attributes.description: The original death benefit (DB) coverage amount requested by the applicant in the initial application.
attributes.references: NAIC Life Insurance Policy Illustration Model Regulation

attributes.name: applied_product_code
attributes.description: The product code originally applied for by the applicant (e.g., Whole Life (WL), Universal Life (UL), Indexed Universal Life (IUL)).

attributes.name: communication_method
attributes.description: The method used to communicate the counter-offer to the applicant or agent. Tracks compliance with timely notification requirements.
attributes.references: State Insurance Regulations on Application Processing

attributes.name: counter_offer_number
attributes.description: Business-readable unique identifier for this counter-offer, used in correspondence with agents and applicants.

attributes.name: counter_offer_status
attributes.description: Current status of the counter-offer in the negotiation workflow. Pending indicates awaiting applicant response; accepted means applicant agreed to modified terms; rejected means applicant declined; expired means response deadline passed; withdrawn means underwriting retracted the offer; superseded means a new counter-offer was issued.

attributes.name: counter_offer_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of modification being offered. Modified coverage indicates reduced face amount; table rating indicates mortality surcharge; flat extra indicates per-thousand charge; exclusion rider indicates specific cause exclusion; product change indicates different product recommendation; combined modification indicates multiple changes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this counter-offer record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and process timing analysis.

attributes.name: decision_rationale
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of the underwriting rationale for the counter-offer, including specific risk factors identified (e.g., elevated blood pressure, family history, hazardous occupation). Used for agent communication and audit trail.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation on Unfair Trade Practices

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the specific exclusion rider attached to the counter-offer (e.g., aviation exclusion, hazardous activity exclusion). Indicates specific causes of death that will not be covered.

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the exclusion rider terms, specifying what causes of death or conditions are excluded from coverage.

attributes.name: face_amount
attributes.description: The modified death benefit (DB) coverage amount offered by underwriting. May be lower than applied amount due to risk assessment findings.
attributes.references: NAIC Life Insurance Policy Illustration Model Regulation

attributes.name: financial_evidence_summary
attributes.description: Summary of financial underwriting findings including income verification, net worth assessment, and financial justification for coverage amount that influenced the counter-offer.

attributes.name: flat_extra_duration_months
attributes.description: The number of months the flat extra charge will apply. Null indicates permanent flat extra for the life of the policy.

attributes.name: flat_extra_per_thousand
attributes.description: The additional premium charge per thousand dollars of coverage, applied for specific temporary or permanent risk factors (e.g., hazardous occupation, avocation).

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date the counter-offer was issued to the applicant or agent. Marks the start of the response period.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation on Unfair Claims Settlement Practices

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this counter-offer record was last updated. Tracks changes through the negotiation workflow.

attributes.name: medical_evidence_summary
attributes.description: Summary of key medical evidence findings from Attending Physician Statement (APS), Medical Information Bureau (MIB) reports, and other medical underwriting sources that influenced the counter-offer decision.
attributes.references: HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164

attributes.name: modal_premium_amount
attributes.description: The premium amount per payment period under the counter-offer terms, reflecting the modified risk class, table rating, flat extra, and coverage amount.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation on Policy Illustrations

attributes.name: nar_calculation_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Amount at Risk (NAR) Calculation Amount
attributes.description: The calculated Net Amount at Risk (NAR) for the counter-offer terms, representing the insurance company's exposure (death benefit minus cash value). Used in reinsurance cession and risk-based capital (RBC) calculations.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes and comments related to the counter-offer negotiation, including agent feedback, applicant questions, and underwriting clarifications.

attributes.name: premium_mode
attributes.description: The premium payment frequency for the counter-offer terms (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly). May differ from originally applied mode due to underwriting requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation on Policy Illustrations

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_class
attributes.description: The reinsurance cession class assigned to this counter-offer for automatic treaty placement or facultative submission. Determines reinsurance pricing and terms.

attributes.name: reinsurance_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether facultative or automatic reinsurance placement is required for this counter-offer due to retention limits or risk characteristics. True if reinsurance is needed.

attributes.name: rejection_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the reason the applicant rejected the counter-offer (e.g., premium too high, coverage amount insufficient, product not suitable). Used for Not In Good Order (NIGO) analysis and process improvement.

attributes.name: rejection_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of why the applicant rejected the counter-offer, captured from agent notes or applicant feedback.

attributes.name: response_date
attributes.description: The date the applicant or agent provided their acceptance or rejection response. Null if no response received.

attributes.name: response_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which the applicant must accept or reject the counter-offer. After this date, the offer expires and the application may be declined.
attributes.references: State Insurance Regulations on Application Processing

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the source underwriting workbench system that created this counter-offer record (e.g., RGAX AURA, Swiss Re Magnum). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: table_rating_code
attributes.description: The table rating assigned if the counter-offer includes a mortality surcharge (e.g., Table B, Table D). Represents incremental risk above standard mortality.

attributes.name: table_rating_factor
attributes.description: The numeric multiplier associated with the table rating (e.g., 1.25 for 25% mortality increase). Used in Cost of Insurance (COI) rate calculations.

products.name: exclusion_rider
products.description: Underwriting exclusion rider record documenting specific conditions, activities, or causes of death excluded from coverage as a condition of policy approval. Captures exclusion type (aviation, avocation, specific disease/condition, war), exclusion description, effective date, whether the exclusion is permanent or reviewable, review date, and the underwriting decision that generated the exclusion. Feeds into policy issuance to ensure exclusion riders are attached to issued policies.
products.reference: NAIC Policy Form Filing; State DOI Exclusion Rider Standards

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_id
attributes.description: Primary key for exclusion_rider

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the new business application that generated this exclusion rider during underwriting decisioning.

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the issued policy to which this exclusion rider is attached. Populated after policy issuance.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, ACORD AL3 Standard

attributes.name: insurance_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Exclusion riders produce policy endorsement documents with specific contract language. Business process: policy contract assembly and claims adjudication require linking riders to their endorsement do

attributes.name: policy_form_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy_form_approval. Business justification: Exclusion riders must be filed and approved in each jurisdiction before use. Regulatory requirement: form filing compliance for exclusion rider language. Links exclusion rider to form approval authori

attributes.name: primary_exclusion_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underwriter who made the decision to apply this exclusion rider as a condition of policy approval.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Underwriting Audit Trail

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reinsurance.cession. Business justification: Exclusion riders on policies must be tracked at cession level for claims administration. Reinsurer needs to know what exclusions apply to ceded risk to properly adjudicate claims and calculate recover

attributes.name: report_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reporting.report_period. Business justification: Exclusion riders are tracked by period for mortality experience studies, claims analysis, underwriting quality metrics, and risk selection effectiveness. Required for actuarial experience studies and

attributes.name: underwriting_decision_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underwriting decision that resulted in this exclusion rider being required as a condition of approval.

attributes.name: aps_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Attending Physician Statement (APS) or medical evidence that documented the condition or risk leading to this exclusion rider.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Medical Information Bureau (MIB) Guidelines

attributes.name: claims_notification_text
attributes.description: Standardized text to be displayed to claims examiners when a claim is filed on a policy with this exclusion rider, alerting them to verify the cause of death against the exclusion terms.
attributes.references: Claims Adjudication Guidelines, NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this exclusion rider record was first created in the underwriting system, typically during the underwriting decision process.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this exclusion rider becomes effective, typically the policy issue date or the date of a policy change that added the exclusion.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Contract Terms

attributes.name: excluded_cause_of_death
attributes.description: Specific cause of death or medical condition excluded from death benefit payment (e.g., 'death resulting from aviation activities', 'death due to pre-existing heart condition').
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Claims Adjudication Guidelines

attributes.name: exclusion_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific condition, activity, cause of death, or circumstance excluded from coverage under this rider. This text appears in the policy contract.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Contract Language

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_code
attributes.description: Standard code identifying the type of exclusion rider (e.g., AVN for aviation, WAR for war exclusion, DIS for specific disease exclusion).
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Company Product Filing

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_name
attributes.description: Standard name of the exclusion rider as filed with regulatory authorities and printed on the policy contract.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, State Insurance Department Filings

attributes.name: exclusion_rider_status
attributes.description: Current status of this exclusion rider: active (currently in force on the policy), removed (removed following review or policy change), expired (reached expiration date), superseded (replaced by a different exclusion or policy change).
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Administration Guidelines

attributes.name: exclusion_scope
attributes.description: Scope of the exclusion: death_benefit_only (excludes only death benefit for specified cause), all_benefits (excludes all policy benefits), specific_rider (excludes benefits under a specific rider such as Accidental Death Benefit (ADB) or waiver of premium).
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Contract Terms

attributes.name: exclusion_type
attributes.description: Category of exclusion: aviation (piloting, skydiving), avocation (hazardous hobbies), medical_condition (specific disease or condition), occupational_hazard (dangerous occupation), war_military (war, military service), geographic_region (travel to high-risk areas).

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this exclusion rider expires or is scheduled to be removed. Null if the exclusion is permanent or has no scheduled expiration.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Contract Terms

attributes.name: jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Two-letter state or jurisdiction code where this exclusion rider is filed and approved for use (e.g., CA for California, NY for New York).
attributes.references: NAIC State Codes, State Insurance Departments

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this exclusion rider record, capturing updates to status, review dates, or other attributes.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: medical_director_approval_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusion rider required and received approval from the company medical director. True if medical director approval was obtained.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Underwriting Authority Matrix

attributes.name: mib_code
attributes.description: Medical Information Bureau (MIB) code associated with the medical condition or risk factor that triggered this exclusion rider.

attributes.name: nar_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Amount at Risk (NAR) Impact Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusion rider affects the Net Amount at Risk (NAR) calculation for reinsurance cession and Cost of Insurance (COI) rate determination. True if NAR calculation is impacted.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Reinsurance Treaty Agreement

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form underwriting notes providing additional context, rationale, or special instructions related to this exclusion rider decision.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Underwriting Documentation Standards

attributes.name: permanence_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the exclusion is permanent for the life of the policy, reviewable after a specified period, or conditional based on future evidence or circumstances.

attributes.name: policy_contract_language
attributes.description: Full legal text of the exclusion rider as it appears in the policy contract document, including all terms, conditions, and definitions.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, State Insurance Department Filing

attributes.name: premium_impact_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of premium reduction (if any) resulting from the application of this exclusion rider. Positive values indicate premium savings to the policyholder due to reduced coverage.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Actuarial Pricing Guidelines

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the state insurance department filing that approved this exclusion rider form for use in the applicable jurisdiction.
attributes.references: State Insurance Department, NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: reinsurance_acceptance_status
attributes.description: Status of reinsurer acceptance of this exclusion rider: not_applicable (no reinsurance notification required), pending (awaiting reinsurer response), accepted (reinsurer accepted exclusion), rejected (reinsurer rejected exclusion), modified (reinsurer proposed alternative terms).
attributes.references: Reinsurance Treaty Agreement, NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: reinsurance_notification_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reinsurer must be notified of this exclusion rider per the reinsurance treaty terms. True if notification is required.
attributes.references: Reinsurance Treaty Agreement, NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date on which this exclusion rider was removed from the policy following a successful review or policy change. Null if the exclusion is still in force.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation, Policy Servicing Guidelines

attributes.name: removal_reason
attributes.description: Reason for removal of this exclusion rider (e.g., 'improved health confirmed by updated APS', 'cessation of excluded activity', 'policy anniversary review').

attributes.name: review_criteria
attributes.description: Specific criteria or evidence required for review of this exclusion (e.g., 'clean medical records for 5 years', 'cessation of aviation activities', 'updated Attending Physician Statement (APS)').

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for underwriting review of this exclusion rider to determine if it can be removed or modified based on updated evidence. Null if exclusion is permanent.

attributes.name: review_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusion rider is eligible for future review and potential removal based on improved health or changed circumstances. True if reviewable, False if permanent.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system that created this exclusion rider record (e.g., 'RGAX AURA', 'Swiss Re Magnum', 'Underwriting Workbench').

attributes.name: stoli_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusion rider was applied due to Stranger-Originated Life Insurance (STOLI) concerns or suspicious circumstances. True if STOLI-related.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Act on STOLI, State Insurance Regulations

products.name: impairment_guide
products.description: Reference catalog of medical impairments and underwriting rating guidelines used to assess mortality and morbidity risk for specific health conditions. Stores impairment code, impairment name (e.g., Type 2 Diabetes, Coronary Artery Disease, Sleep Apnea), ICD-10 code mapping, standard rating action (table rating range, flat extra range, decline threshold), age and severity modifiers, and source (company manual or reinsurer guide). Provides the authoritative underwriting manual reference for medical risk classification.
products.reference: Brackenridge's Medical Selection of Life Risks; Reinsurer Underwriting Manuals; ICD-10

attributes.name: impairment_guide_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the impairment guide entry. Primary key for the impairment guide reference catalog.

attributes.name: mortality_table_id

attributes.name: state_regulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.state_regulation. Business justification: Impairment guidelines must comply with state unfair discrimination laws and rating restrictions (e.g., HIV/AIDS, genetic information, disability). Business process: state regulatory compliance for med

attributes.name: age_band_max
attributes.description: Maximum age (in years) for which this impairment rating guideline applies. Null indicates no upper age limit for this guideline.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Actuarial Mortality Tables

attributes.name: age_band_min
attributes.description: Minimum age (in years) for which this impairment rating guideline applies. Enables age-specific risk assessment and rating adjustments.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Actuarial Mortality Tables

attributes.name: clinical_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field containing additional clinical context, risk factors, or underwriting considerations for this impairment. May include treatment protocols, prognosis factors, or comorbidity interactions.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Medical Director Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this impairment guide record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: decline_threshold_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this impairment at the specified severity level triggers an automatic decline recommendation. True if the condition is uninsurable under standard or substandard terms.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this impairment guideline becomes active and applicable for underwriting decisions. Supports temporal validity and guideline versioning.

attributes.name: evidence_requirements
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of required medical evidence for underwriting this impairment (e.g., APS, lab results, ECG, stress test, specialist report). Drives underwriting workbench workflow and evidence ordering.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Medical Information Bureau (MIB) Guidelines

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this impairment guideline is superseded or retired. Null indicates the guideline is currently active with no planned expiration.

attributes.name: flat_extra_duration_months
attributes.description: Duration in months for which the flat extra charge applies. Null indicates permanent flat extra. Used for temporary impairments with expected recovery or stabilization.

attributes.name: flat_extra_per_thousand_max
attributes.description: Maximum flat extra charge per thousand dollars of NAR for this impairment. Defines the upper bound of flat extra rating range.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Actuarial Pricing Basis

attributes.name: flat_extra_per_thousand_min
attributes.description: Minimum flat extra charge per thousand dollars of Net Amount at Risk (NAR) applied for this impairment, expressed in dollars. Used for temporary or permanent additional mortality risk.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Actuarial Pricing Basis

attributes.name: gender_applicability
attributes.description: Gender for which this impairment guideline applies. Certain conditions have gender-specific mortality or morbidity risk profiles.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Actuarial Mortality Tables

attributes.name: guideline_source
attributes.description: Origin of the underwriting guideline for this impairment. Indicates whether the rating is based on internal company manual, reinsurer medical guide, industry best practice, or medical director judgment.
attributes.references: Company Underwriting Manual, Reinsurer Medical Manuals

attributes.name: guideline_version

products.name: treaty_risk_pricing
products.description: This association product represents the reinsurance pricing agreement between a specific risk classification and a treaty schedule. It captures the negotiated rates, allowances, and terms that apply when ceding business of a particular risk class under a specific reinsurance treaty. Each record links one risk_class to one treaty_schedule with pricing attributes that exist only in the context of this reinsurance arrangement.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, a single treaty schedule defines pricing for MULTIPLE risk classifications (Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard, Substandard tables, etc.), and each risk class can have different negotiated rates across MULTIPLE reinsurance treaties with different reinsurers. The business actively manages a pricing grid where YRT rates, coinsurance percentages, table rating factors, and allowances are negotiated and maintained per treaty-risk class combination. This is operational data that reinsurance teams create, update, and query regularly.

attributes.name: allowance_percentage

attributes.name: coinsurance_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the policy's face amount or account value ceded to the reinsurer for this risk class under this treaty. Varies by risk class as higher-risk classes may have different coinsurance terms.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

products.name: application_document
products.description: This association product represents the document package relationship between underwriting applications and insurance documents. It captures the specific role, submission status, and version of each document required for or submitted with an application. Each record links one application to one document with attributes that exist only in the context of this application-document relationship, such as the document's role in the application (e.g., application form, illustration, medical records, replacement form), submission status, and whether the document is required or optional.. Existence Justification: In life insurance underwriting operations, applications require multiple documents (application form, illustrations, medical records, APS, beneficiary designations, replacement forms, financial statements) to complete the underwriting review process. Simultaneously, the same document can be shared across multiple concurrent applications for the same applicant or related parties (e.g., medical records from one exam used for multiple policies, financial statements for concurrent applications). The business actively manages document packages as a core underwriting workflow, tracking which documents are required, received, reviewed, and approved for each application, with specific roles and statuses that belong to the application-document relationship rather than to either entity alone.

attributes.name: document_role
attributes.description: The specific role or purpose this document serves within the application package. Examples include application form, illustration, replacement form, beneficiary designation, medical records, APS (Attending Physician Statement), financial statement, identity verification documents. This attribute exists only in the context of the application-document relationship because the same document (e.g., medical records) may serve different roles in different applications.

This is relationship-specific because document requirements vary by application characteristics (e.g., medical exam required for high face amounts).

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date when this specific document was submitted or received for this application. This is relationship-specific because the same document may be submitted on different dates for different applications (e.g., medical records used for concurrent applications).

attributes.name: version_number

products.name: application_party_role
products.description: This association product represents the Role relationship between party and application. It captures the participation of a party in an underwriting application in a specific capacity (proposed insured, owner, payor, beneficiary, guardian, attorney-in-fact). Each record links one party to one application with role-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this participation: role type, signature details, consent status, and role sequence for ordering multiple parties in the same role.. Existence Justification: In life insurance underwriting, applications inherently involve multiple parties in different capacities: the proposed insured, policy owner (often different from insured), premium payor (may differ from owner), primary and contingent beneficiaries (multiple allowed), and legal representatives (guardians for minors, attorneys-in-fact, trustees for trust-owned policies). Conversely, a single party participates in multiple applications over their lifetime as they apply for different policies, and the same party may serve in different roles across applications (e.g., insured on one application, beneficiary on another). Underwriters actively manage party participation by verifying signatures, consent status, insurable interest, and role-specific requirements for each party-application combination.

products.name: program_rule_configuration
products.description: This association product represents the configuration relationship between underwriting programs and underwriting rules. It captures how specific rules are applied within the context of each program, including rule priority, program-specific overrides, and temporal applicability. Each record links one program to one rule with attributes that define how that rule behaves within that specific program context.. Existence Justification: Underwriting programs and rules have a genuine operational many-to-many relationship in life insurance. A single underwriting program (e.g., Simplified Issue Term) uses dozens or hundreds of rules to evaluate applications, and a single rule (e.g., 'Type 2 Diabetes with HbA1c >9%') is reused across multiple programs (Term, Whole Life, Guaranteed Issue) with program-specific configurations. The business actively manages Program Rule Configurations where the same rule behaves differently across programs—different priorities, different rating actions, different evidence requirements. This is not an analytical correlation; underwriting operations teams explicitly configure, version, and maintain these rule sets as a core operational activity.

products.name: claimant
products.description: Master record for every individual or entity asserting a claim against a life insurance policy or annuity contract. Distinct from the policyholder domain's insured record — a claimant is the party making the claim demand, which may be a beneficiary, the insured themselves (DI/LTC/living benefit), an estate, or a trust (ILIT). Captures claimant name, SSN/TIN, relationship to insured, contact information, KYC/AML verification status, identity document references, and legal capacity (individual, estate, trust, minor with guardian). products.name: beneficiary_verification
products.description: Operational record tracking the formal verification process for each beneficiary or claimant asserting entitlement to claim proceeds. Links to the claimant record (claims domain) and references the beneficiary designation from the policyholder domain to validate entitlement. Captures verification type (identity, insurable interest, legal standing, minor guardianship, estate probate, trust/ILIT validation), verification status, documents requested and received, MIB check results, AML/BSA screening outcome, OFAC sanctions check status, KYC verification results, verification examiner, verification date, and any adverse findings requiring escalation. products.name: claim_investigation
products.description: Tracks all formal investigation workflows for claims requiring scrutiny beyond standard adjudication, including Special Investigations Unit (SIU) referrals, contestability reviews, and field investigations. CONTESTABILITY: covers claims within the 2-year contestability window — application misrepresentation findings, medical history discrepancies, MIB report findings, and rescission recommendations. FRAUD/SIU: covers fraud referral triggers, SIU case numbers, fraud indicator scoring, law enforcement referrals, state DOI fraud bureau filings (per NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act), and NICB database checks. GENERAL INVESTIGATION: covers cause-of-death investigations, APS requests, MIB record reviews, STOLI/stranger-originated life insurance investigations, and field investigations. Records investigation type, escalation level (standard, SIU referral, law enforcement), assigned investigator, investigation open/close dates, findings summary, investigation disposition (substantiated, unsubstantiated, closed without action, rescind policy, pay in full, reduce benefit), and regulatory reporting obligations. SSOT for all claim investigation, fraud referral, and contestability review activity within the claims domain.

products.name: adjudication
products.description: Core transactional record capturing the formal adjudication decision for a claim, including full denial documentation and adverse action lifecycle when applicable. Records adjudication outcome (approved, denied, partially approved, pended, rescinded), adjudication date, examiner ID, decision basis (policy provisions applied: suicide exclusion, contestability, misrepresentation, exclusion riders), benefit amount approved, supervisor review flag, and authority level applied. For approved claims: captures the selected settlement method and election details (elected option, payment frequency, tax withholding preference, beneficiary signature confirmation) as the SSOT for the adjudication-time settlement decision. For denial outcomes: captures denial reason codes (per NAIC and state DOI standards), policy provision cited, denial letter generation date, adverse action notice compliance flag, claimant appeal rights disclosure, external review referral flag, internal review completion date, and litigation hold management. Supports state prompt payment law compliance and DOI complaint tracking. SSOT for all claim adjudication decisions and adverse actions within the claims domain. Note: settlement election details here record the decision-time election; claim_payment records the execution-time disbursement details.

products.name: db_calculation
products.description: Death Benefit (DB) calculation record capturing the actuarial and contractual computation of the total death benefit payable for a life insurance claim. Tracks base face amount, accumulated dividends, paid-up additions, outstanding loan balance deductions, premium arrears deductions, ADB (Accidental Death Benefit) rider amount, GMDB (Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefit) floor for variable products, interest on delayed payment, and net DB payable. Supports WL, UL, IUL, VUL, and term product benefit calculations. Provides the authoritative benefit amount feeding the adjudication and payment records.

attributes.description: Total dividends accumulated on the policy that are left on deposit with the insurer and payable as part of the death benefit. Applicable primarily to participating whole life policies.

attributes.description: Additional death benefit payable if the insured's death was caused by a covered accident. Typically doubles or triples the base face amount. Zero if death was not accidental or rider not in force.

attributes.name: interest_on_delayed_payment
attributes.description: Interest accrued on the death benefit from the date of death to the date of payment, as required by state insurance regulations. Typically calculated at the statutory interest rate.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act, State Insurance Codes

attributes.name: nar_amount
attributes.description: The net amount at risk to the insurer, calculated as the death benefit minus the policy reserve or account value. Critical for reinsurance cession calculations and risk management.

attributes.name: net_db_payable
attributes.description: The final net death benefit amount payable to beneficiaries after all additions and deductions. This is the authoritative benefit amount that feeds adjudication and payment records.

attributes.name: outstanding_loan_balance
attributes.description: Total outstanding policy loan principal and accrued interest that must be deducted from the gross death benefit. Loans reduce the net amount payable to beneficiaries.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702, NAIC Model Policy Loan Provisions

attributes.name: paid_up_additions
attributes.description: Additional insurance purchased with policy dividends that increases the total death benefit. Common in whole life policies with dividend reinvestment options.

attributes.name: premium_arrears
attributes.description: Unpaid premiums owed by the policyholder at the time of death, including any grace period premiums. Deducted from the gross death benefit.

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Type of life insurance product for which the death benefit is calculated. WL=Whole Life, UL=Universal Life, IUL=Indexed Universal Life, VUL=Variable Universal Life, term=Term Life, SPIA=Single Premium Immediate Annuity.

attributes.name: recalculation_reason
attributes.description: Reason for recalculating the death benefit if this is a subsequent version. Examples include additional information received, correction of errors, beneficiary dispute resolution, or appeal.

attributes.name: reinsurance_ceded_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the death benefit that is ceded to reinsurers under reinsurance treaties. Used to calculate the net retained liability and reinsurance recoverables.

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the death benefit calculation was reviewed and approved by a senior examiner or manager.

attributes.name: statutory_interest_rate
attributes.description: The interest rate mandated by state law for calculating interest on delayed death benefit payments. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5%).

attributes.name: suicide_clause_applied_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the suicide exclusion clause was applied to this calculation. If death occurred within the suicide exclusion period (typically 2 years), only premiums paid may be returned instead of the full death benefit.

attributes.name: total_deductions
attributes.description: Sum of all deductions from the gross death benefit, including outstanding loan balance, premium arrears, and any other policy-specific deductions.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this death benefit calculation record was last modified.

products.name: living_benefit_claim
products.description: Consolidated claim detail record for all living-insured benefit claims including Disability Income (DI), Long-Term Care (LTC), Accelerated Death Benefit (ADB), chronic/critical illness riders, GMIB/GMWB annuity guarantees, and Waiver-of-Premium (WP) claims. Captures claim subtype, triggering event (disability onset, terminal/chronic/critical illness diagnosis, ADL impairment, cognitive impairment), elimination period tracking, benefit calculation basis, payment frequency and duration, ongoing eligibility verification requirements, medical documentation (ICD-10 codes, APS, functional capacity evaluations), disability definition applied (own-occ, any-occ, modified own-occ), care setting (for LTC: home health, assisted living, nursing facility), Social Security offset (for DI), coordination of benefits with Medicare/Medicaid (for LTC), tax treatment (IRC 101(g) for ADB), waiver trigger and premium amount waived (for WP), inflation protection adjustment (for LTC), and termination/recovery events. Extends the core claim record with type-specific attributes while sharing the common claim lifecycle. SSOT for all non-death-benefit claim detail within the claims domain — replaces standalone DI, LTC, and waiver-of-premium claim records.

attributes.name: diagnosis_description

attributes.name: elimination_period_days

attributes.name: elimination_period_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the elimination period was satisfied and benefit payments became eligible to commence. Calculated as elimination_period_start_date plus elimination_period_days.

attributes.name: elimination_period_satisfied_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the elimination period has been fully satisfied. True indicates the waiting period is complete and benefits are eligible for payment; False indicates the elimination period is still in progress.

attributes.name: elimination_period_start_date

attributes.name: functional_capacity_evaluation_date

attributes.name: inflation_protection_rate

attributes.name: monthly_benefit_amount

attributes.name: next_eligibility_verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the next periodic eligibility verification (re-certification) is required to confirm ongoing qualification for living benefits. Common for DI and LTC claims to ensure continued impairment. Null if no periodic verification is required.

attributes.name: payment_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which living benefit payments are disbursed to the claimant. Common frequencies include monthly (most common for DI and LTC), quarterly, annual, lump sum (for ADB or critical illness), or as incurred (for reimbursement-based LTC).

attributes.name: recovery_date
attributes.description: The date on which the insured recovered from the disability or condition, resulting in termination of living benefit payments. Null if no recovery has occurred or if claim terminated for other reasons.

attributes.name: reinsurance_recoverable_amount
attributes.description: The amount recoverable from reinsurers for this living benefit claim under applicable reinsurance treaties. Represents the ceded portion of claim payments. Zero if no reinsurance applies.

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: The actuarial reserve amount established for this living benefit claim to cover estimated future benefit payments. Updated periodically based on claim experience and actuarial assumptions. Used for statutory and GAAP financial reporting.

attributes.name: social_security_offset_amount

IRC Section 7702B governs qualified Long-Term Care (LTC) benefits (tax-free up to per diem limits). Other benefits may be taxable income.

products.name: claim_status_history
products.description: Immutable audit trail of every status transition and significant activity event for a claim throughout its lifecycle. Records status change events (submitted, under review, pended, investigation, approved, denied, payment issued, closed, reopened), prior and new status, change timestamp, changed-by user ID, change reason code, activity type (status change, examiner note, communication, diary entry, SLA milestone), note text for activity entries, confidentiality flag (attorney-client privilege, SIU sensitive), and associated references. Enables SLA compliance monitoring, regulatory reporting of claim processing timelines, dispute resolution, and complete claim file narrative for audits. Supports state DOI prompt payment law compliance tracking (typically 30-day adjudication windows). SSOT for claim lifecycle audit trail, activity log, and examiner notes within the claims domain.
products.reference: NAIC Prompt Payment Model Act / State DOI Regulations

attributes.name: claim_status_history_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each claim status history record. Primary key for the immutable audit trail of claim lifecycle events.

attributes.name: adjudication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claims.adjudication. Business justification: Status history events related to adjudication (adjudication completed, decision rendered, approval issued) should reference the specific adjudication record. This provides granular audit trail linking

attributes.name: appeal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claims.appeal. Business justification: Status history events related to appeal (appeal filed, appeal under review, appeal decision rendered) should reference the specific appeal record. This provides audit trail of appeal lifecycle events.

attributes.name: claim_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent claim record. Links this status history event to the specific claim being tracked.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: System user identifier of the person or automated process that triggered this status change or activity. Supports audit trail and accountability requirements.

attributes.name: insurance_document_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this activity to a document in the document management system. Enables retrieval of supporting documentation for audit and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: activity_note_text
attributes.description: Free-form text note entered by the examiner or system describing the activity, decision rationale, or communication summary. Critical for claim file narrative and regulatory exam defense.
attributes.references: State DOI Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: activity_type
attributes.description: Type of activity or event recorded in this history entry. Distinguishes between status transitions, examiner notes, communications, diary entries, Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestones, and document receipt events.

attributes.name: attorney_client_privilege_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this activity record is protected by attorney-client privilege. Used to restrict disclosure during regulatory examinations and litigation discovery processes.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Evidence Article V

attributes.name: change_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the business reason for the status change or activity. Maps to internal reason code reference tables for consistent categorization.

attributes.name: change_reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable explanation of the reason for the status change or activity. Provides business context for audit review and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: changed_by_role
attributes.description: Business role or job function of the user at the time of the event (e.g., Claims Examiner, Senior Adjudicator, Special Investigations Unit (SIU) Investigator, System Administrator). Supports role-based audit analysis.

attributes.name: changed_by_user_name
attributes.description: Full name of the user who performed the status change or activity. Denormalized for audit reporting and dispute resolution without requiring user table joins.

attributes.name: communication_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the communication occurred (phone, email, postal mail, fax, customer portal, in-person). Supports channel effectiveness analysis and regulatory documentation requirements.

attributes.name: communication_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the external party involved in the communication. Supports complete claim file documentation for regulatory exams and litigation defense.
attributes.references: State DOI Market Conduct Examination Standards

attributes.name: communication_party_type
attributes.description: Type of external party involved in the communication (claimant, beneficiary, agent, attorney, attending physician, investigator, reinsurer, other). Enables stakeholder engagement tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: claimant|beneficiary|agent|attorney|physician|investigator|reinsurer|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: communication_type
attributes.description: Direction of communication activity: inbound (received from claimant, beneficiary, agent, or third party) or outbound (sent to external party). Applicable when activity_type is communication.

attributes.name: confidential_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this activity record contains attorney-client privileged information or Special Investigations Unit (SIU) sensitive content. Controls access and disclosure in regulatory exams and litigation discovery.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this status history record was inserted into the data warehouse. Distinct from status_change_timestamp which reflects the business event time. Supports data lineage and Extract Transform Load (ETL) auditing.

attributes.name: diary_completed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the diary entry has been completed or resolved. False indicates an open diary item requiring follow-up action.

attributes.name: diary_due_date
attributes.description: Follow-up date for diary entries. Indicates when the examiner should review the claim for pending items or next actions. Supports workflow management and Service Level Agreement (SLA) tracking.

attributes.name: document_type
attributes.description: Type of document received or generated (e.g., Attending Physician Statement (APS), death certificate, beneficiary identification, investigative report). Applicable when activity_type is document_received.

attributes.name: event_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of status change and activity events within a claim lifecycle. Enables chronological reconstruction of claim history.

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: The claim status after this event. For non-status-change activities, this field contains the current status at the time of the activity. Supports state-at-time queries.

attributes.name: prior_status
attributes.description: The claim status immediately before this event. Null for the initial claim submission event. Enables tracking of status transitions and workflow progression.

attributes.name: siu_sensitive_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this activity is part of a fraud investigation by the Special Investigations Unit (SIU). Restricts access to authorized fraud investigators and legal counsel.

attributes.name: sla_actual_date
attributes.description: Actual date when this Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestone was completed. Compared against target date to measure compliance and identify process bottlenecks.

attributes.name: sla_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestone was met within the target timeframe. False indicates a breach of service level commitments or regulatory prompt payment requirements.

attributes.name: sla_milestone_type
attributes.description: Type of Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestone reached (e.g., initial contact, acknowledgment sent, decision rendered, payment issued). Supports compliance tracking for state prompt payment laws.

attributes.name: sla_target_date
attributes.description: Target date by which this Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestone should be completed. Used to calculate compliance with state Department of Insurance (DOI) prompt payment requirements (typically 30-day adjudication windows).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that created this status history record (e.g., Guidewire ClaimCenter, Majesco Claims). Supports data lineage tracking in multi-system environments.

attributes.name: source_transaction_reference
attributes.description: Unique transaction identifier from the source operational system. Enables traceability back to the originating system for reconciliation and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: status_change_date
attributes.description: Calendar date of the status change or activity event. Supports day-level reporting and aggregation for state Department of Insurance (DOI) regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: status_change_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the status change or activity event occurred. Critical for Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance monitoring and regulatory prompt payment law tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation for Prompt Payment of Claims

attributes.name: system_generated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this activity was automatically generated by the claims system (e.g., automated Service Level Agreement (SLA) milestone tracking, workflow triggers) versus manually entered by a user.

products.name: appeal
products.description: Tracks the formal appeal process when a claimant contests a claim denial or partial payment decision. Captures appeal type (internal administrative review, external independent review, DOI complaint, litigation, arbitration), appeal filing date, appeal deadline, appeal basis stated by claimant, additional evidence submitted, reviewing examiner or committee, appeal decision, appeal decision date, outcome (upheld, overturned, modified), and appeal exhaustion status. Manages the regulatory appeal timelines mandated by state DOI regulations and ERISA for group products. Feeds compliance domain for DOI complaint reporting. SSOT for all claim appeal and dispute resolution activity within the claims domain.
products.reference: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices / ERISA / State DOI

attributes.name: arbitration_case_number

products.name: unclaimed_property
products.description: Tracks life insurance claim proceeds and matured benefits that cannot be disbursed due to lost beneficiary contact, unlocated beneficiaries, or uncashed checks, subject to state escheatment laws. Captures policy reference, benefit amount, last known beneficiary contact date, due diligence outreach attempts (NAIC Model 695 compliance), escheatment eligibility date, state of domicile for escheatment, escheatment filing date, remittance to state unclaimed property fund, and DMF (Death Master File) match status. Supports compliance with NAIC Model Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act and state-specific dormancy periods. SSOT for all unclaimed property and escheatment tracking within the claims domain.
products.reference: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act / State Escheatment Laws

attributes.name: unclaimed_property_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the unclaimed property record. Primary key for tracking life insurance claim proceeds and matured benefits that cannot be disbursed due to lost beneficiary contact or unlocated beneficiaries.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_party_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.party. Business justification: Due diligence process for unclaimed property requires linking beneficiary to party master for address updates, contact attempts, and state escheatment filing. Removes denormalized beneficiary name fie

attributes.name: claim_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated claim record if the unclaimed property originated from a death benefit or other claim settlement that could not be disbursed.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: claim_payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claims.claim_payment. Business justification: Unclaimed property should reference the original claim_payment that was issued but returned/unclaimed. This links the escheatment record to the specific payment attempt. Business pattern: payment issu

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying life insurance policy or annuity contract from which the unclaimed benefit originated.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: insured_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.insured. Business justification: Escheatment compliance and DMF matching require linking unclaimed property records to insured master for death verification, beneficiary search, and state reporting. Removes denormalized insured attri

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Escheatment events require GL entries to reclassify claim liabilities to unclaimed property liability accounts and record state remittances. This is a distinct accounting event mandated by state uncla

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Escheatment processing and due diligence requirements vary by product type, state approval specifications, and dormancy period rules. Product plan determines state of domicile and regulatory complianc

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Unclaimed property requires annual escheatment filings to state treasurers/comptrollers. Insurance operations must link unclaimed property records to regulatory filings for compliance tracking and aud

attributes.name: beneficiary_address_line_1
attributes.description: Primary street address line for the last known address of the beneficiary. Used for due diligence outreach mailings per NAIC Model 695 requirements.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_address_line_2
attributes.description: Secondary street address line (apartment, suite, unit) for the last known address of the beneficiary.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_city
attributes.description: City of the last known address of the beneficiary. Used for due diligence outreach and state domicile determination.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_claim_amount
attributes.description: The dollar amount paid to the beneficiary when the unclaimed property was successfully claimed. May include interest accrued per state law.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_claim_date
attributes.description: Date when the beneficiary successfully claimed the unclaimed benefit, either directly from the insurer (before escheatment) or from the state unclaimed property fund (after escheatment).
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the last known address of the beneficiary. Determines whether state escheatment laws apply or if international unclaimed property protocols are required.

attributes.name: beneficiary_postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code of the last known address of the beneficiary. Used for due diligence outreach mailings.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: beneficiary_state_province
attributes.description: State or province of the last known address of the beneficiary. Critical for determining the applicable state escheatment law and dormancy period.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: benefit_amount
attributes.description: The total dollar amount of the unclaimed benefit including death benefit, account value (AV), accumulated interest, and any guaranteed minimum death benefit (GMDB) or guaranteed minimum income benefit (GMIB) amounts. Excludes interest accrued post-escheatment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date when the unclaimed property record was closed, either due to successful beneficiary claim, escheatment to state, or administrative closure (e.g., benefit amount below state minimum threshold).
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: closure_reason
attributes.description: Reason for closing the unclaimed property record: beneficiary paid (successfully claimed), escheated to state (remitted to state fund), below threshold (amount below state minimum reporting threshold), duplicate record (consolidated with another record), or administrative error (record created in error).
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the unclaimed property record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the benefit amount. Typically USD for US-domiciled policies.

attributes.name: dmf_match_date
attributes.description: Date when the Death Master File (DMF) match was performed or confirmed. Used to establish the timeline for due diligence and escheatment eligibility.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: dmf_match_status
attributes.description: Result of the Death Master File (DMF) comparison to identify deceased insureds whose beneficiaries have not claimed benefits. Matched indicates a confirmed death record; no match indicates insured not found in DMF; pending indicates search in progress; manual review indicates ambiguous results requiring human verification.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: dormancy_period_years
attributes.description: Number of years of inactivity required before the property becomes eligible for escheatment, as defined by the applicable state unclaimed property law. Typically ranges from 3 to 5 years depending on jurisdiction.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: due_diligence_attempts_count
attributes.description: Total number of outreach attempts made to locate the beneficiary, including certified mail, phone calls, email, and database searches. NAIC Model 695 requires documented reasonable efforts.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: due_diligence_completed_date
attributes.description: Date when all required due diligence outreach efforts were completed, regardless of outcome. Establishes compliance with NAIC Model 695 requirements prior to escheatment.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: due_diligence_initiated_date
attributes.description: Date when the insurer initiated due diligence outreach efforts to locate the beneficiary, as required by NAIC Model 695. Must occur before escheatment eligibility date.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: due_diligence_method
attributes.description: Description of the due diligence methods employed to locate the beneficiary: certified mail, phone outreach, email, address verification services, public records search, social media search, or third-party locator services. Must meet NAIC Model 695 reasonable search standards.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: due_diligence_outcome
attributes.description: Result of the due diligence outreach efforts: beneficiary located (contact established), no response (outreach delivered but no reply), address invalid (mail returned), deceased beneficiary (beneficiary also deceased), or refused claim (beneficiary declined benefit).

attributes.name: escheatment_eligibility_date
attributes.description: Date when the unclaimed property becomes eligible for escheatment to the state unclaimed property fund, calculated as last known contact date plus the applicable state dormancy period. Triggers due diligence and reporting obligations.

attributes.name: escheatment_filing_date
attributes.description: Date when the unclaimed property report was filed with the applicable state unclaimed property administrator. Typically occurs annually by a state-mandated deadline (e.g., November 1).
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: escheatment_remittance_amount
attributes.description: The actual dollar amount remitted to the state unclaimed property fund. May differ from the original benefit amount due to interest accrual, administrative fees, or partial claims.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: escheatment_remittance_date
attributes.description: Date when the unclaimed benefit amount was remitted to the state unclaimed property fund. Typically occurs shortly after the filing date per state law.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: last_known_contact_date
attributes.description: Date of the last confirmed contact with the beneficiary or policyholder (premium payment, correspondence, service request, or other affirmative action). Establishes the start of the dormancy period for escheatment eligibility per state law.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, special circumstances, or case-specific details related to the unclaimed property record, due diligence efforts, or escheatment process.

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: The externally-known policy or contract number associated with the unclaimed benefit. Used for beneficiary outreach and state reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: state_claim_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned by the state unclaimed property administrator when the property is escheated. Used for tracking and reconciliation if the beneficiary later claims the property from the state.
attributes.references: NAIC Model 695 Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act

attributes.name: state_of_domicile
