products.name: claims_cession
products.description: This association product represents the operational cession of claim risk from the ceding company to one or more reinsurers under specific treaty terms. It captures the financial and contractual relationship between a specific claim and a specific treaty, including the portion of risk ceded, amounts recoverable, and cession status. Each record links one claim to one treaty with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific risk transfer transaction.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, a single claim can be ceded to multiple reinsurance treaties simultaneously based on layered reinsurance structures, product line coverage, and retention limits. For example, a $5M death benefit claim may have $1M retained, $2M ceded to Treaty A (base coverage), $1M ceded to Treaty B (rider coverage), and $1M ceded to Treaty C (excess of loss). Conversely, each treaty covers thousands of claims over its lifetime. The business actively manages each cession as a distinct operational record with specific amounts, percentages, statuses, and recovery tracking.

attributes.name: claims_cession_id
attributes.description: Primary key for claims_cession

attributes.name: cession_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this specific cession record. Primary key for the cession association.

attributes.name: claim_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the claim whose risk is being ceded under this treaty

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the reinsurance treaty under which this claim risk is ceded

attributes.name: ceded_amount
attributes.description: Total face amount or Net Amount at Risk (NAR) ceded to the reinsurer for this claim under this treaty. Calculated based on cession percentage and claim amount. Identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: cession_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this cession record: pending (awaiting reinsurer acknowledgment), active (in force), settled (reinsurer has paid recovery), disputed (disagreement on terms or amount), cancelled (cession reversed). Identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this cession record was created in the reinsurance system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this cession record (ceded_amount, recoverable_amount). Must align with treaty_currency from the treaty.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this specific cession became effective and the risk transfer to the reinsurer commenced for this claim under this treaty. Identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the ceding company notified the reinsurer of this claim cession under this treaty. Required for treaty compliance and recovery timing.

attributes.name: percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the claim risk ceded to the reinsurer under this treaty. Represents the proportional share of risk transferred for this specific claim-treaty combination. Identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: recoverable_amount
attributes.description: Amount expected to be recovered from the reinsurer for this specific claim under this specific treaty. May differ from ceded_amount based on treaty terms, allowances, and claim adjudication. Identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: recovery_amount_received
attributes.description: Actual amount received from the reinsurer for this cession. May differ from recoverable_amount due to disputes, adjustments, or treaty allowances.

attributes.name: recovery_received_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reinsurer paid the recoverable amount to the ceding company for this cession. Null if recovery is pending or disputed.

attributes.name: reinsurance_recoverable_amount
attributes.description: Amount expected to be recovered from reinsurers under ceded reinsurance treaties for this claim. [Moved from claim: This attribute in the claim product represents the TOTAL recoverable amount across ALL treaties. The per-treaty recoverable amount belongs in the cession association as recoverable_amount. The claim-level attribute should be derived as SUM(cession.recoverable_amount) for all cessions of that claim.]

attributes.name: reinsurer_claim_number
attributes.description: External claim reference number assigned by the reinsurer for tracking this cession. Used in correspondence and recovery processing with the reinsurer.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this cession record was last modified.

products.name: investigation_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between claim_investigation and employee. It captures the operational reality that complex claim investigations require multi-disciplinary teams with specialized roles (lead investigator, field investigator, medical reviewer, fraud analyst, legal counsel). Each record links one claim_investigation to one employee with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment: the specific role performed, assignment dates, hours allocated to the investigation, investigation phase responsibility, and percentage of overall investigation responsibility for cost allocation and workload management purposes.. Existence Justification: Complex claim investigations in life insurance require multi-disciplinary teams with specialized roles: lead investigators manage the case, field investigators conduct on-site work, medical reviewers analyze APS and MIB data, fraud analysts score risk indicators, and legal counsel advises on rescission and regulatory reporting. Each employee works multiple investigations concurrently, and each investigation has multiple team members. The business actively manages these assignments with role definitions, time allocation, phase responsibility, and cost allocation percentages.

attributes.name: investigation_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this investigation assignment record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: claim_investigation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the claim investigation being staffed. Each assignment record associates one investigation with one employee in a specific role.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the employee assigned to the investigation. Each assignment record captures one employee's participation in one investigation.

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: Date this employee was assigned to this investigation in this role. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data. Used for workload tracking and investigation timeline analysis.

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date this employee's assignment to this investigation ended (investigation closed, role transferred, employee reassigned). Null for active assignments. Supports historical tracking of investigation team changes.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this assignment. Tracks whether the employee is actively working this investigation, temporarily on hold, completed their portion, or was reassigned.

attributes.name: hours_actual
attributes.description: Actual hours this employee worked on this investigation. Used for cost tracking, variance analysis, and workload management. Compared against hours_allocated for budget control.

attributes.name: hours_allocated
attributes.description: Total hours allocated or budgeted for this employee's work on this investigation. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data. Used for cost allocation and capacity planning.

attributes.name: investigation_phase
attributes.description: The phase of the investigation lifecycle for which this employee has primary responsibility. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data. Supports phase-based workload and timeline tracking.

attributes.name: investigation_role
attributes.description: The specific role this employee performs in this investigation. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data. Critical for understanding team composition and responsibility allocation.

attributes.name: primary_assignment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the primary/lead assignment for this investigation (typically the lead investigator). Used to identify the main point of contact and primary responsible party.

attributes.name: responsibility_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of overall investigation responsibility allocated to this employee (0.00 to 100.00). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data. Used for cost allocation across team members and workload balancing.

products.name: interpleader_team_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of internal employees to interpleader case teams. It captures the operational reality that complex interpleader litigation requires coordinated multi-disciplinary teams (claims counsel, litigation managers, compliance officers, senior adjusters) working on the same case, with each employee managing multiple concurrent interpleader cases. Each record links one interpleader case to one employee with role, time allocation, and responsibility tracking required for legal cost management and case coordination.. Existence Justification: Interpleader litigation cases require multi-disciplinary case teams with specialized roles (claims counsel, litigation managers, compliance officers, senior adjusters). Each complex interpleader case has multiple employees working on it simultaneously with distinct responsibilities, and each employee manages multiple concurrent interpleader cases. The business actively manages these team assignments with role definitions, time tracking, and responsibility allocation for legal cost management and case coordination.

attributes.name: interpleader_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the interpleader case being staffed

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: Date the employee was assigned to this interpleader case team. Used for workload tracking and cost allocation.

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date the employee's assignment to this case ended. Null for active assignments. Used for historical team composition tracking.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current status of this team assignment. Tracks lifecycle of employee involvement in the case.

attributes.name: external_counsel_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this employee is coordinating with external legal counsel for this case. Used for cost allocation and communication tracking.

attributes.description: Specific aspect of the interpleader case this employee is responsible for (e.g., 'court filings', 'claimant negotiations', 'regulatory compliance', 'document discovery'). Enables coordination and prevents duplication.

attributes.name: role_in_case
attributes.description: Specific functional role the employee performs on this interpleader case team. Determines responsibility areas and approval authority.

domains.name: billing
domains.description: SSOT for all premium billing, collection, and payment processing activities. Owns premium schedules, modal billing (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly), grace period management, lapse administration, reinstatement processing, NSF handling, EFT/ACH payment records, APE calculations, premium allocation across policy components (base, riders, COI), and automatic premium loan (APL) triggers.

Serves as the authoritative source for what is owed and when for each policy. Owned by the Billing and Premium Collection System (Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing).

Billing configuration must reference the approved form number to ensure premiums charged match DOI-approved rates. Required for rate

attributes.description: Reference to the insurance policy for which this premium schedule is defined. Links the billing schedule to the master policy record in the Policy Administration System.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Premium Policy In Force Policy Id
attributes.description: FK to policy.in_force_policy.in_force_policy_id — Premium billing schedules must be linked to the policy they bill for. Without this FK, billing cannot determine premium amounts, modal frequencies, or grace period triggers for a specific policy.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agent.producer. Business justification: Premium schedules need writing producer attribution for commission calculations, persistency tracking, and producer book-of-business reporting. Standard requirement for producer compensation systems a

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded description of the reason for the most recent amendment to this premium schedule (e.g., 'modal frequency change', 'face amount increase', 'rider addition', 'reinstatement'). Populated when schedule_version > 1. Supports audit trail and policyholder service history.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: ape_amount
attributes.description: Annual Premium Equivalent (APE) representing the annualized value of the modal premium. Calculated as the modal premium multiplied by the modal frequency factor (e.g., monthly × 12). Used for new business reporting, sales performance measurement, and actuarial valuation inputs per industry APE conventions.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Annual Statement; IFRS 17

attributes.name: apl_activated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) feature is currently active on this schedule. When True, the billing system has been configured to execute APL draws upon premium non-payment. Distinct from apl_eligible which reflects product eligibility.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: apl_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy is eligible for Automatic Premium Loan (APL) processing. When True, the billing system will automatically trigger a policy loan to cover an unpaid premium before the policy lapses, provided sufficient cash surrender value (CSV) exists. Applicable to whole life and universal life products.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; IRC Section 7702; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: base_premium_amount
attributes.description: The annualized premium attributable to the base policy coverage only, excluding rider premiums. Used for premium allocation across policy components (base vs. riders) and for Cost of Insurance (COI) calculations in universal life products.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: billing_day_of_month
attributes.description: The day of the month on which the premium billing notice is generated and/or the EFT/ACH debit is initiated. Valid values are 1 through 28 (capped at 28 to avoid month-end variability). Stored in the billing system as the recurring debit/invoice trigger date.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NACHA ACH Operating Rules

attributes.name: billing_method
attributes.description: The method by which premiums are collected from the policyholder. 'direct_bill' sends invoices directly to the insured; 'eft_ach' uses Electronic Funds Transfer / Automated Clearing House (EFT/ACH) for automatic bank debits; 'payroll_deduction' applies to employer-sponsored plans; 'list_bill' is used for group or association billing; 'bank_draft' is a pre-authorized bank withdrawal. Drives payment processing workflow in Sapiens BillingPro / Majesco Billing.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NACHA ACH Operating Rules; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: billing_notice_preference
attributes.description: The policyholder's preferred channel for receiving premium billing notices and payment reminders. 'paper' sends physical mail; 'email' sends electronic notices; 'sms' sends text message reminders; 'portal' delivers notices via the insurer's online self-service portal; 'none' suppresses notices (e.g., for EFT/ACH auto-pay enrollees).
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; State Department of Insurance e-delivery regulations

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this premium schedule record was first created in the billing system. Represents the business event time of schedule establishment, which typically coincides with policy issuance or a subsequent schedule amendment. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this premium schedule (e.g., USD). Required for multi-currency policy administration and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this premium schedule becomes binding and the first premium is due. Aligns with the policy issue date or the date of a schedule amendment (e.g., modal frequency change, face amount change).
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this premium schedule ends. Null for open-ended schedules (e.g., whole life). Populated for term policies at the end of the premium-paying period or upon policy maturity.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: grace_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days after the premium due date during which the policy remains in force without payment. Standard grace period is 30 or 31 days per NAIC model regulations. After expiry of the grace period without payment, the policy enters lapse administration processing.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: guideline_annual_premium
attributes.business_glossary_term: Guideline Annual Premium (GAP) — Guideline Premium Test (GPT)
attributes.description: The Guideline Annual Premium (GAP) used in the Guideline Premium Test (GPT) under IRC Section 7702 to determine whether the policy qualifies as life insurance for tax purposes. Calculated by the actuarial system. Premiums paid must not exceed the greater of the GAP or the Guideline Single Premium (GSP).
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702; IRS regulations; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: lapse_date
attributes.description: The date on which the policy lapsed due to non-payment of premium beyond the grace period. Null for active schedules. Populated by the lapse administration module of the billing system. Critical for lapse experience studies and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: last_paid_date
attributes.description: The date through which the policy is paid up based on the most recent premium payment received. Used to determine the paid-to date for policy servicing, lapse calculations, and reinstatement eligibility.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limited_pay_years
attributes.description: Number of years over which premiums are payable for limited-pay policies (e.g., 10-pay, 20-pay, paid-up at 65). Null when premium_paying_period is not 'limited_pay'. Used to calculate the schedule expiry date and for MEC testing under IRC Section 7702A.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: mec_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy has been classified as a Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) under IRC Section 7702A. 'non_mec' policies retain favorable tax treatment; 'mec' policies are subject to LIFO tax treatment on distributions; 'pending_test' indicates the 7-pay test is in progress. Critical for tax compliance reporting to the IRS.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; IRS Publication 575; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: modal_factor
attributes.description: The multiplier applied to the annual premium to derive the modal premium amount for the selected billing frequency. Reflects the cost of installment billing (e.g., monthly factor ≈ 0.0875, quarterly ≈ 0.26, semi-annual ≈ 0.51, annual = 1.0). Stored for audit and recalculation purposes.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: modal_frequency
attributes.description: The payment frequency selected by the policyholder for premium remittance. Determines the billing cycle and the modal premium amount applied. Standard life insurance modal frequencies per ACORD and NAIC conventions.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: modal_premium_amount
attributes.description: The scheduled premium amount due at each billing interval as determined by the selected modal frequency. Reflects the base policy premium plus any rider premiums and modal loading factor. This is the gross amount billed to the policyholder per billing cycle.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; IRC Section 7702; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The date on which the next scheduled premium payment is due from the policyholder. Updated by the billing engine after each successful payment or following a reinstatement. Critical for grace period tracking and lapse administration.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: nsf_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) / returned payment events on this premium schedule. Used to assess payment reliability, trigger EFT/ACH suspension, and support fraud detection and AML monitoring per FinCEN BSA requirements.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Operating Rules; FinCEN BSA/AML requirements; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: nsf_fee_amount
attributes.description: The fee charged to the policyholder per Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) / returned payment event, as defined in the policy contract and state regulations. Used for billing reconciliation and policyholder account management.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Operating Rules; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: paid_to_date
attributes.description: The date through which the policy coverage is fully funded by premiums received. Distinct from last_paid_date in that it reflects the coverage period end rather than the transaction date. Used in policy servicing, reinstatement, and lapse administration workflows.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: premium_paying_period
attributes.description: Defines the duration over which premiums are payable under the policy contract. 'whole_life' requires premiums for the life of the insured; 'limited_pay' specifies a fixed number of years; 'single_premium' is a one-time payment; 'term_to_age' requires premiums until a specified attained age. Drives schedule expiry and Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) testing.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702; IRC Section 7702A (MEC); ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: reinstatement_date
attributes.description: The date on which a lapsed policy's premium schedule was reinstated following payment of overdue premiums and satisfaction of reinstatement requirements. Null for schedules that have never lapsed. Used in reinstatement processing and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Life Insurance Act; State Department of Insurance regulations

attributes.name: rider_premium_amount
attributes.description: The annualized premium attributable to all policy riders combined (e.g., Accidental Death Benefit (ADB), Waiver of Premium, Long-Term Care (LTC) rider). Supports premium allocation reporting and rider-level profitability analysis.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this premium schedule, as assigned by the Billing and Premium Collection System (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro). Used in policyholder correspondence, billing notices, and reconciliation with payment records.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the premium schedule. Drives billing engine behavior: 'active' schedules generate billing notices; 'suspended' schedules are on hold (e.g., waiver of premium); 'lapsed' indicates non-payment past grace period; 'reinstated' follows successful reinstatement processing; 'cancelled' or 'terminated' are end-states. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|suspended|lapsed|reinstated|cancelled|terminated — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Sapiens BillingPro lifecycle states

attributes.name: schedule_version
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version number for this premium schedule record. Incremented each time the schedule is amended (e.g., modal frequency change, face amount change, rider addition/removal). Supports audit trail and temporal data management in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: seven_pay_premium_limit
attributes.description: The maximum cumulative premium that can be paid in the first seven policy years without triggering Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) classification under IRC Section 7702A. Calculated by the actuarial system and stored here for billing compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: IRC Section 7702A; IRS Publication 575; Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this premium schedule record was sourced (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro, Majesco Billing). Used for data lineage tracking, ETL reconciliation, and Silver Layer data quality management in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this premium schedule record in the billing system. Updated on any field change including status transitions, payment date updates, and schedule amendments. Used for incremental ETL processing and audit trail in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: waiver_of_premium
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Waiver of Premium (WP) benefit is currently active on this schedule, typically triggered by the insured's disability. When True, scheduled premiums are waived and the billing engine suspends premium collection while keeping the policy in force.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Disability Income Regulation; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: waiver_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Waiver of Premium (WP) benefit became effective for this schedule. Null when waiver_of_premium is False. Used to track the duration of the waiver period and for actuarial experience studies.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Disability Income Regulation; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards
