attributes.description: The Modified Coinsurance (ModCo) reserve adjustment amount representing the difference between the ceded reserve and the funds withheld balance. Captures the periodic settlement adjustment required under ModCo treaties to reconcile reserve movements with withheld asset performance.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944; IFRS 17; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: movement_amount
attributes.description: The change in ceded reserve between the prior valuation date and the current valuation date. Positive values indicate reserve increases (additional cession); negative values indicate reserve releases. Used in bordereaux reporting and reinsurance settlement calculations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944 (LDTI); IFRS 17; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Bordereaux Reporting Module

attributes.name: net_ceded_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The net ceded reserve amount after applying any ModCo adjustments, experience refund reserves, or other treaty-specific offsets. Represents the final net reserve position ceded to the reinsurer for financial reporting purposes.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944 (LDTI); NAIC SAP; IFRS 17; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: prior_period_reserve_amount
attributes.description: The ceded reserve amount as of the prior valuation date. Used to calculate the reserve movement (change in ceded reserve) for the current period, which drives reinsurance premium settlements and LDTI/IFRS 17 ceded reserve roll-forward reporting.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944 (LDTI); IFRS 17; NAIC SAP; Actuarial Valuation System (AXIS; Prophet)

attributes.name: rbc_credit_amount
attributes.description: The Risk-Based Capital (RBC) credit recognized by the ceding company for this ceded reserve position. Represents the reduction in required capital resulting from the reinsurance arrangement. Supports RBC optimization reporting and ORSA (Own Risk and Solvency Assessment).
attributes.references: NAIC RBC (Risk-Based Capital) Framework; NAIC ORSA Model Act; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: reinsurer_share_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the policy reserve ceded to this reinsurer under the treaty. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.900000 = 90%). Used in proportional coinsurance and quota share treaties to calculate the reinsurer's share of reserves and premiums.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The financial reporting period to which this reserve record belongs, expressed as quarter (e.g., Q12024, Q42023) or full year (e.g., FY2023). Used for LDTI, PBR, IFRS 17, and NAIC statutory reporting period alignment.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944 (LDTI); IFRS 17; NAIC Annual Statement; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: reserve_method
attributes.description: The actuarial reserving method applied to calculate the ceded reserve. 'net_premium' = Net Premium Reserve method; 'gross_premium' = Gross Premium Reserve method (LDTI); 'commissioners_reserve' = NAIC Commissioners Reserve Valuation Method (CRVM); 'pbr_deterministic' = PBR deterministic scenario; 'pbr_stochastic' = PBR stochastic scenario. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: net_premium|gross_premium|commissioners_reserve|pbr_deterministic|pbr_stochastic|crvm|net_single_premium — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC VM-20 PBR; FASB ASC 944 LDTI; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP); Actuarial Valuation System (AXIS; Prophet)

attributes.name: reserve_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this reinsurance reserve record, used in bordereaux reporting and reinsurer settlement statements. Typically assigned by the reinsurance management system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS or RGA AURA).
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Bordereaux Reporting Module

attributes.name: reserve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reinsurance reserve by structural arrangement. 'traditional_ceded' = standard ceded reserve transferred to reinsurer; 'funds_withheld' = reserve retained by ceding company under funds withheld coinsurance; 'modco_adjustment' = Modified Coinsurance (ModCo) reserve adjustment; 'experience_refund_reserve' = reserve held for experience refund obligations; 'retrocession_ceded' = reserve ceded under retrocession arrangement.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944; IFRS 17; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the reinsurance reserve balance was or is expected to be settled with the reinsurer. Used for cash flow planning, ALM coordination, and reinsurance recoverable tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Settlement Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: Current settlement status of the reinsurance reserve balance with the reinsurer. 'pending' = awaiting settlement; 'settled' = fully settled in current period; 'disputed' = under dispute with reinsurer; 'partially_settled' = partially settled; 'voided' = record voided due to error or treaty termination.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Settlement Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this reinsurance reserve record was sourced (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS, RGA AURA Reinsurance). Supports data lineage and ETL (Extract Transform Load) traceability in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Reinsurance Management System; RGA AURA Reinsurance; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this reinsurance reserve record was last modified. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and SOX compliance requirements for financial reporting records in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 404; NAIC Annual Statement; FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The as-of date for which the ceded reserve is calculated. Represents the actuarial valuation date used in reserve calculations (e.g., quarter-end or year-end). Aligns with LDTI, PBR, and IFRS 17 reporting periods.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944 (LDTI); NAIC PBR (Principle-Based Reserving); IFRS 17; Actuarial Valuation System (AXIS; Prophet; MoSes)

attributes.name: valuation_system
attributes.description: The actuarial valuation system used to calculate this ceded reserve (e.g., AXIS, Prophet, MoSes). Supports data lineage, audit traceability, and reconciliation between actuarial and reinsurance management systems.
attributes.references: Actuarial Valuation System (MoSes; AXIS; Prophet); NAIC PBR; FASB ASC 944 (LDTI)

products.name: experience_refund
products.description: Tracks experience refund calculations and payments from reinsurers to Life Insurance when actual mortality or morbidity experience is more favorable than the treaty pricing assumptions. Captures refund period, treaty reference, reinsurer, actual claims incurred, expected claims per treaty, experience margin, refund amount, and payment status. Supports profit-sharing and experience-rated treaty management.

attributes.name: experience_refund_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each experience refund record in the reinsurance domain. Primary key for the experience_refund data product.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Experience refund calculations require actuarial review and approval for financial accuracy and regulatory compliance. Tracks who approved the calculation for SOX controls, professional liability, and

attributes.name: experience_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.experience_study. Business justification: Experience refunds are calculated based on experience studies comparing actual vs expected mortality/lapse. Essential for treaty experience rating, profit sharing, and reinsurer settlement calculation

attributes.name: insurance_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: Experience refunds require calculation worksheets, supporting schedules, mortality experience reports, payment vouchers, and approval documentation. Financial settlement and treaty profit-sharing proc

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Experience refund accounting requires GL posting for revenue recognition, treaty profitability analysis, and GAAP/SAP reporting. Finance teams book refunds as recoverable income and reconcile to treat

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Experience refunds are reportable items in statutory annual statements affecting surplus calculations and reinsurance credit. Must be disclosed in Schedule S and reconciled to treaty terms for regulat

attributes.name: reinsurance_dispute_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reinsurance.reinsurance_dispute. Business justification: Experience refund calculations can be disputed by either party regarding mortality ratio calculations, expected claims methodology, or deficit carryforward treatment. The table currently has 'dispute_

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance treaty under which this experience refund is calculated. Links to the governing treaty terms, pricing assumptions, and experience-rating provisions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: reinsurer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance counterparty (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re) responsible for issuing the experience refund payment to Life Insurance.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: actual_claims_incurred
attributes.description: Total dollar amount of claims actually incurred under the ceded block during the experience period, including both paid claims and Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) reserves. Core input to the experience refund calculation.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944; IBNR Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP No. 25)

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the experience refund calculation was formally approved by the authorized reinsurance or actuarial team at Life Insurance, prior to invoicing the reinsurer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: bordereaux_period
attributes.description: The bordereaux reporting period (e.g., 2024-Q1, 2024-H1, 2024-12) to which this experience refund is associated for reinsurer reporting and reconciliation purposes.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: calculation_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the experience refund amount was formally calculated by the actuarial or reinsurance administration team. Represents the principal real-world event date for this transaction.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944 LDTI

attributes.name: ceded_nar
attributes.description: The total Net Amount at Risk (NAR) ceded to the reinsurer under the treaty during the experience period. NAR is the difference between the death benefit and the policy reserve, representing the reinsurer's actual mortality exposure used in experience refund calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards; FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this experience refund record was first created in the reinsurance management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this experience refund record (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency treaty management.

attributes.name: deficit_carryforward
attributes.description: Cumulative unfavorable experience deficit carried forward from prior periods under the treaty, which must be recovered before a positive experience refund becomes payable. Tracks the running deficit balance per treaty experience-rating provisions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which a disputed experience refund was formally resolved between Life Insurance and the reinsurer. Null if no dispute exists or dispute is still open.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: expected_claims_per_treaty
attributes.description: Total dollar amount of claims expected under the ceded block during the experience period, as defined by the treaty pricing assumptions (e.g., mortality tables, morbidity rates). Serves as the benchmark against which actual experience is measured.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP No. 25)

attributes.name: expense_allowance
attributes.description: The reinsurer's contractual expense loading deducted from the experience margin before computing the refund amount. Covers the reinsurer's administrative, acquisition, and overhead costs as defined in the treaty.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: experience_margin
attributes.description: The difference between expected claims per treaty and actual claims incurred, representing the favorable (positive) or unfavorable (negative) deviation from treaty pricing assumptions. A positive margin indicates favorable experience eligible for refund.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: experience_period_months
attributes.description: Duration in months of the experience period covered by this refund calculation. Typically 12 months for annual experience refunds but may be shorter for mid-year or stub-period calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: experience_rating_basis
attributes.description: The contractual basis on which experience is rated for refund purposes under the treaty: pooled (across multiple ceding companies), individual (specific to Life Insurance's block), aggregate (all lines combined), or corridor (refund only within defined experience bands).
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: gaap_recoverable_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) Recoverable Amount
attributes.description: The experience refund amount recognized as a reinsurance recoverable asset on Life Insurance's GAAP balance sheet under FASB ASC 944, reflecting the portion of the refund that meets GAAP asset recognition criteria.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944; GAAP Generally Accepted Accounting Principles; LDTI Long Duration Targeted Improvements

attributes.name: ibnr_included
attributes.business_glossary_term: Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) Included Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) reserves are included in the actual claims incurred figure used for this experience refund calculation. True if IBNR is included; False if only paid claims are used.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP No. 25)

attributes.name: mortality_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of actual claims incurred to expected claims per treaty for the experience period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.75 = 75% A/E ratio). A ratio below 1.0 indicates favorable mortality experience eligible for refund.
attributes.references: Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP No. 25); NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional commentary, actuarial assumptions, or operational notes related to this experience refund record, such as methodology changes, restatements, or treaty amendment references.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: The contractual date by which the reinsurer is required to remit the experience refund payment to Life Insurance, as specified in the treaty settlement terms.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: The method by which the experience refund payment is settled between the reinsurer and Life Insurance, such as wire transfer, check, netting against premiums payable, or offset against other treaty balances.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: payment_received_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the experience refund payment was received from the reinsurer. Used to track settlement timeliness and support accounts receivable reconciliation.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current status of the experience refund payment from the reinsurer, tracking whether payment is pending, invoiced, received, partially received, overdue, or waived.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: profit_share_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this experience refund qualifies as a profit-sharing arrangement under the treaty terms, as distinct from a pure experience-rated refund. Affects accounting treatment under GAAP and SAP.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: The net dollar amount of the experience refund payable by the reinsurer to Life Insurance, calculated by applying the treaty refund formula (e.g., refund percentage applied to the experience margin after deducting the reinsurer's risk charge and expense loading).
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: refund_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this experience refund, as assigned by the reinsurance management system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS or RGA AURA). Used for bordereaux reporting and reinsurer correspondence.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: refund_percentage
attributes.description: The contractual percentage of the favorable experience margin that is returned to Life Insurance as an experience refund, as specified in the treaty profit-sharing or experience-rating provisions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: refund_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last day of the experience period covered by this refund calculation. Together with refund_period_start_date, defines the observation window for actual versus expected claims comparison.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: refund_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first day of the experience period covered by this refund calculation. Defines the beginning of the observation window over which actual claims are measured against treaty pricing assumptions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: refund_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the experience refund record, tracking progression from calculation through approval, invoicing, and payment settlement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: calculated|pending_approval|approved|invoiced|paid|disputed|voided — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: refund_type
attributes.description: Classification of the experience refund indicating whether it is based on favorable mortality experience, favorable morbidity experience, or a combined mortality and morbidity basis as defined in the treaty.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: reinsurance_premium_earned
attributes.description: Total reinsurance premiums earned by the reinsurer during the experience period under the treaty. Used as a key input in experience-rated refund formulas to determine the reinsurer's revenue base against which claims are measured.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; FASB ASC 944; SAP Statutory Accounting Principles

attributes.name: risk_charge
attributes.description: The reinsurer's contractual risk charge deducted from the experience margin before computing the refund amount. Represents the reinsurer's compensation for bearing mortality or morbidity risk under the treaty.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: sap_recoverable_amount
attributes.description: The experience refund amount recognized as a reinsurance recoverable under Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP) for NAIC regulatory reporting purposes. May differ from GAAP recoverable due to statutory accounting rules.
attributes.references: SAP Statutory Accounting Principles; NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational reinsurance management system from which this experience refund record originated (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS, RGA AURA Reinsurance, or manual entry). Supports data lineage and ETL traceability.

attributes.name: source_system_refund_ref
attributes.description: The native identifier or reference number assigned to this experience refund record in the originating reinsurance management system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS transaction ID or RGA AURA refund reference). Enables cross-system reconciliation.

attributes.name: treaty_year
attributes.description: The year of the reinsurance treaty to which this experience refund applies, used to align refund calculations with the correct treaty pricing table and experience-rating corridor for that treaty year.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this experience refund record was last modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory compliance.

products.name: automatic_binding_limit
products.description: Reference table defining the automatic binding limits per treaty, plan code, risk class, and age band — the maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission. Captures treaty reference, plan code, risk class, age band, automatic binding limit amount, jumbo limit, and effective date. Drives the cession routing logic determining whether a risk qualifies for automatic or facultative placement.

attributes.name: automatic_binding_limit_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each automatic binding limit record. Primary key for the automatic_binding_limit reference table. [_canonical_skip_reason: Entity role is REFERENCE_LOOKUP — defines maximum face amounts auto-ceded per treaty/plan/risk-class/age-band combination; exempt from per-role minimums.]
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Binding limit changes affect underwriting authority and risk exposure, requiring documented approval by authorized underwriting management. Critical for delegation of authority validation, SOX control

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Automatic binding limits are defined per product plan. Essential for automatic vs. facultative decisioning in underwriting workflow, capacity management, and treaty compliance. Plan_code is denormaliz

attributes.name: pricing_basis_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.pricing_basis. Business justification: Automatic binding limits are set based on pricing bases, mortality assumptions, and risk assessment. Required for automatic capacity determination and treaty design.

attributes.name: prior_limit_automatic_binding_limit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the previous version of this binding limit record that was superseded by the current record. Enables traversal of the amendment history chain for audit and regulatory review purposes.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance treaty under which this automatic binding limit applies. Links the limit record to the governing treaty agreement between the ceding company and the reinsurer.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: reinsurer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurer (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re) that is party to the treaty for which this binding limit is defined. Used to identify the counterparty in cession routing decisions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: state_regulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.state_regulation. Business justification: Automatic binding limits must comply with state-specific regulations governing retention requirements, jumbo limit thresholds, and automatic coverage capacity. State regulations define minimum retenti

attributes.name: age_band_max
attributes.description: The maximum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this automatic binding limit row applies. Together with age_band_min, defines the age band dimension of the cession routing matrix.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP); Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: age_band_min
attributes.description: The minimum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this automatic binding limit row applies. Age banding is a standard actuarial practice in reinsurance treaty design as mortality risk and NAR vary significantly by age.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP); Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the business reason for creating or amending this binding limit record (e.g., treaty renegotiation, capacity adjustment, regulatory change, experience-driven repricing). Supports audit trail and governance review.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this binding limit record was formally approved by the authorized approver. Supports governance audit trail and SOX compliance documentation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; NAIC Reinsurance Model Law

attributes.name: automatic_capacity_amount
attributes.description: The total aggregate face amount capacity available under the automatic treaty for new cessions. Once this capacity is exhausted, new risks must be submitted facultatively even if they fall within the per-policy binding limit. Null indicates unlimited capacity.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: binding_limit_amount
attributes.description: The maximum face amount (death benefit) in the treaty currency that can be automatically ceded to the reinsurer under this treaty without requiring facultative submission. Risks with face amounts at or below this threshold qualify for automatic placement. This is the principal quantitative fact of this reference record.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: cession_basis
attributes.description: Indicates whether this limit record governs automatic cessions, facultative cessions, or an automatic-facultative arrangement. Drives the cession routing logic in the Reinsurance Management System to determine placement pathway.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: cession_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the eligible risk (face amount or NAR) that is ceded to the reinsurer under quota-share or coinsurance arrangements. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9000 = 90%). Applicable primarily for coinsurance and quota-share treaty types; may be null for YRT treaties where cession is based on NAR excess over retention.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this automatic binding limit record was first created in the data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the binding limit and jumbo limit amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, CAD). Required for multi-currency treaty arrangements with international reinsurers such as Swiss Re or RGA.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this automatic binding limit record becomes operative for cession routing decisions. New business applications with policy effective dates on or after this date are subject to this limit.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: facultative_threshold_amount
attributes.description: The face amount above the automatic binding limit at which the ceding company must submit the risk facultatively to the reinsurer. Risks between the binding limit and this threshold may be eligible for automatic-facultative placement; risks above this threshold require full facultative submission.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: flat_extra_max
attributes.description: The maximum flat extra premium per thousand of face amount (per mille) that is eligible for automatic cession under this binding limit. Risks with flat extras exceeding this threshold require facultative submission. Null indicates no flat extra restriction.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum)

attributes.name: insured_gender
attributes.description: The gender of the insured to which this binding limit applies. Some treaties define gender-specific binding limits due to mortality differentials. A value of Unisex indicates the limit applies regardless of gender.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA)

attributes.name: is_aviation_excluded
attributes.description: Indicates whether risks involving aviation hazards (private pilot, commercial pilot, or frequent flyer exclusions) are excluded from automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, aviation-rated risks must be submitted facultatively.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum)

attributes.name: is_foreign_national_excluded
attributes.description: Indicates whether foreign nationals (non-US citizens or non-permanent residents) are excluded from automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, policies on foreign nationals must be submitted facultatively regardless of face amount.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; FinCEN AML/BSA Compliance; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA)

attributes.name: is_jumbo_check_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a jumbo limit check (aggregate in-force across all reinsurers on the same life) must be performed before automatic cession is permitted under this binding limit. When True, the cession routing system must query total in-force amounts across all treaties before confirming automatic placement.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: is_mib_check_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Information Bureau (MIB) Check Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Medical Information Bureau (MIB) check is required as a condition of automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, the underwriting workbench must confirm MIB clearance before the risk qualifies for automatic placement.
attributes.references: MIB Group Inc. Data Standards; NAIC Underwriting Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum)

attributes.name: issue_age_basis
attributes.description: The age calculation convention used to determine the insured's age for applying the age band (e.g., Age Last Birthday, Age Nearest Birthday). Must align with the age basis used in the Policy Administration System to ensure consistent cession routing.
attributes.value_regex: Age Last Birthday|Age Nearest Birthday|Age Next Birthday
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP No. 25)

attributes.name: jumbo_limit_amount
attributes.description: The maximum total in-force amount across all reinsurers on a single life (aggregate across all treaties) beyond which the risk is considered a jumbo risk and requires special handling or facultative placement regardless of individual treaty binding limits. Prevents over-concentration of risk on a single life.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: limit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this automatic binding limit record. Active records are used in cession routing. Superseded records have been replaced by a newer version. Expired records are past their termination date. Suspended records are temporarily inactive pending treaty renegotiation.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: nar_basis
attributes.description: Specifies whether the binding limit is applied against the full face amount (death benefit) or the Net Amount at Risk (NAR), which is the death benefit less the policy reserve or account value. NAR-based limits are common in UL and IUL products where the NAR decreases as the account value grows.
attributes.value_regex: Face Amount|Net Amount at Risk|Account Value Excess
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOP); Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: reinsurer_treaty_reference
attributes.description: The reinsurer's own internal reference number or identifier for this treaty and binding limit schedule. Used for reconciliation with reinsurer bordereaux reports and correspondence from partners such as RGA or Swiss Re.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: retention_limit_amount
attributes.description: The maximum face amount the ceding company retains on its own books before ceding the excess to the reinsurer under this treaty. Used in conjunction with the binding limit to determine the ceded portion (face amount minus retention). Supports NAR-based cession calculations.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: risk_class
attributes.description: The underwriting risk classification for which this binding limit applies (e.g., Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard, Substandard). Automatic binding limits typically vary by risk class as higher-risk classifications may have lower automatic limits or require facultative submission.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum); ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: smoker_status
attributes.description: The tobacco/smoker classification of the insured to which this binding limit applies. Smoker and non-smoker populations carry different mortality rates and may have distinct binding limits under the treaty.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum)

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational source system from which this binding limit record was extracted (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, INTERNAL_TREATY_MGMT). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: source_system_limit_ref
attributes.description: The natural key or record identifier assigned to this binding limit record in the originating source system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS internal limit ID or RGA AURA schedule reference). Enables reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the source system.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance Module

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code (USPS abbreviation) for which this binding limit applies, if the limit is state-specific. Null indicates the limit applies in all states. Some states have regulatory restrictions that may affect automatic binding limits.
attributes.references: State Departments of Insurance (all 50 US states); NAIC Model Regulation; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards

attributes.name: table_rating_max
attributes.description: The maximum substandard table rating (e.g., Table A through Table P, or Table 1 through Table 16) eligible for automatic cession under this binding limit. Risks with table ratings exceeding this threshold must be submitted facultatively. Null indicates no table rating restriction.
attributes.references: NAIC Underwriting Standards; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Underwriting Workbench (RGAX AURA / Swiss Re Magnum)

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date on which this automatic binding limit record ceases to be operative. Null indicates the record is currently active with no defined end date. Used to support historical versioning of binding limits as treaties are amended.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Law; ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this automatic binding limit record was last modified in the data platform. Used to detect changes and support incremental processing in the Databricks Silver Layer ETL pipeline.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number for this binding limit record within the same treaty/plan/risk-class/age-band combination. Incremented each time the binding limit is amended. Supports historical audit trail and point-in-time cession routing reconstruction.
attributes.references: ACORD Life & Annuity Data Standards; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

products.name: retention_limit
products.description: Consolidated reference table defining Life Insurance's net retention limits and automatic binding limits by treaty, plan code, risk class, age band, and policy year. Captures limit type (retention per life, retention per policy, automatic binding limit, jumbo limit), limit amount, effective date, and applicable treaty. Includes automatic binding limits per treaty — the maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission — with age/sex/risk class bands and jumbo thresholds. Drives the cession routing decision: risks within retention are kept, risks within automatic binding limits are auto-ceded, and risks exceeding jumbo limits require facultative submission. This is the single source of truth for all retention and automatic binding limit reference data. Supports NAR-based cession calculations and treaty compliance.

attributes.name: retention_limit_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each retention limit record. Primary key for the retention_limit reference table. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — this is a reference/configuration record defining net retention and automatic binding limit thresholds used in cession routing decisions.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Retention limits vary by product plan. Required for cession amount calculation, treaty compliance validation, and retention strategy management. Plan_code and product_line are denormalized; FK enables

attributes.name: pricing_basis_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.pricing_basis. Business justification: Retention limits are established using pricing bases and profitability targets to optimize risk retention vs reinsurance cost. Essential for retention strategy and treaty design.

attributes.name: prior_limit_retention_limit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the immediately preceding version of this retention limit record that was superseded. Enables a linked history chain for audit trail and regulatory review of limit changes over time.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance treaty under which this retention or automatic binding limit applies. Links the limit record to the governing treaty agreement with the reinsurer (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re).
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; NAIC Model Regulation 000

attributes.name: reinsurer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance counterparty (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re, Munich Re) for whom this automatic binding limit or retention schedule applies. Some treaties involve multiple reinsurers with different binding limits per reinsurer.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: age_band_max
attributes.description: The maximum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this retention limit record applies. Combined with age_band_min to define the age band. Null indicates no upper age restriction for this limit record.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: age_band_min
attributes.description: The minimum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this retention limit record applies. Combined with age_band_max to define the age band. Retention and automatic binding limits typically vary by age due to increasing mortality risk at older ages.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this retention limit record was formally approved by the authorized actuarial or reinsurance management authority. Required for SOX compliance and internal governance documentation of limit changes.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation; ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual (typically Chief Actuary, VP Reinsurance, or CRO) who authorized this retention limit record. Supports governance, audit trail, and SOX internal control requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation; ERM Framework

attributes.name: cession_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this limit record governs automatic cessions (risks ceded within treaty terms without individual submission), facultative cessions (risks requiring individual reinsurer approval), or facultative-obligatory arrangements. Automatic binding limits apply only to automatic cession type.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this retention limit record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; FASB ASC 944; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: credit_for_reinsurance_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reinsurer qualifies for credit for reinsurance under applicable state insurance law, allowing the ceding company to take a reserve credit on its statutory balance sheet. Determined by reinsurer licensure status and collateral arrangements.
attributes.references: NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law; State Departments of Insurance; SAP Accounting Principles

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the limit amount is denominated (e.g., USD). Required for multi-currency treaty arrangements and international reinsurance partners.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this retention or binding limit record becomes operative and governs cession routing decisions. Aligns with treaty effective dates and policy year boundaries.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this retention or binding limit record ceases to be operative. Null indicates an open-ended limit with no scheduled expiration. Used in conjunction with effective_date to determine the applicable limit for a given valuation or cession date.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: flat_extra_max
attributes.description: The maximum flat extra premium per thousand of face amount (expressed in dollars per thousand) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with flat extras exceeding this threshold require facultative submission. Null indicates no flat extra restriction.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: gender
attributes.description: Gender classification band to which this retention limit applies. Some treaty structures differentiate retention limits by gender due to mortality table differences. Unisex indicates the limit applies to all genders. Null indicates no gender restriction.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: jumbo_limit_amount
attributes.description: The absolute maximum face amount threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required, regardless of whether the risk falls within the automatic binding limit. Risks exceeding the jumbo limit cannot be automatically ceded and must be individually underwritten by the reinsurer. Null if this record is not of type jumbo_limit.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limit_amount
attributes.description: The principal monetary threshold value for this limit record, expressed in the applicable currency. For retention_per_life and retention_per_policy, this is the maximum net face amount retained by the company. For automatic_binding_limit, this is the maximum face amount that can be auto-ceded. For jumbo_limit, this is the threshold above which facultative submission is mandatory. Drives the cession routing decision engine.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance — Treaty Management Module

attributes.name: limit_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this retention or binding limit configuration within the reinsurance management system (e.g., RET-WL-NS-M-01). Used as the business key for cross-system reference and bordereaux reporting.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance — Treaty Management Module; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: limit_description
attributes.description: Free-text description providing additional context about this retention limit record, including any special conditions, exceptions, or treaty-specific notes that are not captured in structured fields. Used by reinsurance analysts and actuaries for reference.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: limit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the retention limit record. Active records drive live cession routing decisions. Superseded records have been replaced by a newer version. Expired records are past their effective period. Pending records are approved but not yet in effect.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the limit record: retention_per_life (maximum net amount retained across all policies on a single life), retention_per_policy (maximum net amount retained on a single policy), automatic_binding_limit (maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission), or jumbo_limit (threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required regardless of treaty).
attributes.references: NAIC Model Regulation; Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance

attributes.name: nar_basis
attributes.description: Specifies the basis on which the retention limit amount is measured: face_amount (total death benefit face), NAR (Net Amount at Risk — death benefit minus reserve), account_value (for UL/IUL/FIA products), or death_benefit (total contractual death benefit including riders). Drives the NAR-based cession calculation methodology.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: per_life_limit_amount
attributes.description: The maximum total net amount the company will retain across all policies insuring the same life (insured). When total in-force exposure on a single life exceeds this threshold, the excess must be ceded. Critical for managing concentration risk on high-value lives.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: policy_year_max
attributes.description: The maximum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Null indicates the limit applies through the end of the policy term. Used in conjunction with policy_year_min to define the policy year band.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: policy_year_min
attributes.description: The minimum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Some treaties define different retention schedules for early policy years versus later years, particularly for YRT (Yearly Renewable Term) treaties where NAR changes over time.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; RGA AURA Reinsurance; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: rate_table_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the actuarial rate table used to derive the retention limit amounts (e.g., 2017CSO, 2001CSO, company-specific mortality table). Ensures traceability between limit values and the underlying actuarial assumptions used in their derivation.
attributes.references: Actuarial Valuation System — AXIS; Prophet; NAIC Model Regulation; PBR Compliance

attributes.name: rbc_credit_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether cessions made under this retention limit qualify for RBC (Risk-Based Capital) credit under NAIC RBC formula requirements. RBC-eligible cessions reduce the company's required capital, making this flag critical for capital optimization and ORSA reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC RBC Model Act; NAIC Model Regulation; ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: risk_class
attributes.description: Underwriting risk classification band to which this retention limit applies. Retention limits and automatic binding limits typically vary by risk class, as higher-risk classifications carry greater mortality exposure. Null indicates the limit applies across all risk classes.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Model Regulation; MIB Group Standards

attributes.name: smoker_status
attributes.description: Tobacco use classification band to which this retention limit applies. Smoker and non-smoker populations carry materially different mortality rates, often resulting in distinct retention schedules. Null indicates the limit applies regardless of smoker status.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this retention limit record originated (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, INTERNAL_TREATY_MGR). Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: source_system_limit_ref
attributes.description: The native identifier or reference number assigned to this retention limit record in the originating operational system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS internal limit ID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and traceability from the silver layer back to the source system.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS; RGA AURA Reinsurance; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code indicating the jurisdiction to which this retention limit applies. Some state departments of insurance impose specific retention requirements or restrict automatic binding limits. Null indicates the limit applies across all states.
attributes.references: State Departments of Insurance (all 50 US states); NAIC Model Regulation; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: table_rating_max
attributes.description: The maximum substandard table rating (expressed as a letter A–P or numeric percentage, e.g., Table D or 150%) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with table ratings exceeding this threshold require facultative submission regardless of face amount.
attributes.references: Underwriting Workbench — RGAX AURA; Swiss Re Magnum; NAIC Underwriting Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this retention limit record was last modified. Tracks changes to limit amounts, effective dates, or status. Supports audit trail and change management requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; FASB ASC 944; NAIC Model Regulation

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this retention limit record. Incremented each time the limit is revised. Enables tracking of limit changes over time and supports point-in-time queries for historical cession routing validation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: Swiss Re IRIS Treaty Management Module; SOX Compliance; NAIC Model Regulation

products.name: reinsurance_dispute
products.description: Tracks formal disputes between Life Insurance and reinsurers regarding claim recoverables, premium calculations, treaty interpretation, or bordereaux discrepancies. Captures dispute type, disputed amount, originating transaction reference, dispute open date, reinsurer, dispute status, resolution method, and resolution date. Supports reinsurance operations and legal/compliance oversight of counterparty disputes.

attributes.name: reinsurance_dispute_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each reinsurance dispute record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation

attributes.name: assigned_to_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Dispute resolution requires employee ownership for case management, workload tracking, and escalation. Critical for SLA monitoring, performance reviews, and capacity planning. Replaces text field with

attributes.name: claim_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying claim record when the dispute relates to a claim recoverable. Nullable for disputes not originating from a claim event (e.g., premium calculation or bordereaux discrepancy disputes).
attributes.references: NAIC Claim Settlement Practices Model Act; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: complaint_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to correspondence.complaint. Business justification: Some reinsurance disputes escalate to or originate from formal complaints (internal or regulatory). Linking dispute to complaint enables tracking complaint-driven disputes, supports regulatory reporti

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Dispute resolutions and reserve adjustments require GL posting for financial impact tracking, allowance for doubtful accounts, and disclosure. Finance teams post dispute settlements and reserve adjust

attributes.name: legal_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vendor. Business justification: Complex reinsurance disputes often require external legal counsel or arbitration services. Tracks the law firm or arbitration vendor engaged for dispute resolution - necessary for legal spend tracking

attributes.name: market_conduct_exam_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.market_conduct_exam. Business justification: Reinsurance disputes with carriers are frequently identified during market conduct examinations as findings requiring resolution. Examiners review dispute resolution processes, documentation, and fina

attributes.name: originating_communication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to correspondence.communication. Business justification: Reinsurance disputes often originate from or are documented through specific communications (emails, letters, calls) with reinsurers. Tracking the originating communication enables audit trail, regula

attributes.name: premium_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance premium billing record when the dispute relates to a premium calculation discrepancy. Nullable for non-premium disputes.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific cession record that is the subject of or originated the dispute. Provides traceability to the underlying ceded risk transaction.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurance treaty under which the dispute arose. Links to the treaty master record governing the cession terms, retention limits, and settlement obligations.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: reinsurer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reinsurer counterparty (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re) that is party to the dispute. Identifies the external counterparty for legal and operational tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: arbitration_clause_invoked
attributes.description: Indicates whether the formal arbitration clause within the reinsurance treaty has been invoked for this dispute. True when arbitration proceedings have been formally initiated per treaty terms.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; AAA Arbitration Rules for Insurance Industry

attributes.name: bordereaux_period
attributes.description: The reporting period (e.g., 2024-Q1 or 2024-03) of the bordereaux submission that is the subject of or associated with the dispute. Relevant for bordereaux discrepancy and premium calculation dispute types.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this dispute record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance requirements under SOX and NAIC data governance standards.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; NAIC Data Governance Standards; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: credit_for_reinsurance_at_risk
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dispute places the statutory credit for reinsurance at risk, which could affect the cedant's balance sheet and surplus under SAP. Triggers coordination with the actuarial and finance teams.
attributes.references: NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law #785; SAP; NAIC Model Regulation #786

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary amounts on this dispute record are denominated (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Aligns with the treaty currency.

attributes.name: dispute_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the dispute, including the specific point of contention, the basis for Life Insurance's position, and any relevant factual background. Supports legal review and counterparty negotiations.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy

attributes.name: dispute_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the dispute, assigned by the Reinsurance Management System (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS or RGA AURA Reinsurance) at dispute creation. Used in all correspondence with the reinsurer counterparty.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the dispute within the reinsurance operations workflow. Tracks progression from initial filing through resolution or withdrawal.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: dispute_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the dispute. Indicates whether the disagreement concerns a claim recoverable amount, a reinsurance premium calculation, treaty language interpretation, a bordereaux reporting discrepancy, an allowance calculation, or a Net Amount at Risk (NAR) calculation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: claim_recoverable|premium_calculation|treaty_interpretation|bordereaux_discrepancy|allowance_calculation|nar_calculation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: disputed_amount
attributes.description: The gross monetary amount under dispute as initially asserted by Life Insurance. Represents the full value of the disagreement before any negotiation or adjustment. Expressed in the treaty currency.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; FASB ASC 944; SAP

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the dispute was escalated to a higher authority (e.g., senior management, legal counsel, or formal arbitration). Null if the dispute has not been escalated. Supports SLA monitoring and governance reporting.
attributes.references: Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: Narrative explanation of why the dispute was escalated, such as failure to reach agreement within the standard resolution window, material financial exposure, or legal complexity. Null if not escalated.
attributes.references: Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: ibnr_reserve_impact_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) Reserve Impact Amount
attributes.description: Estimated actuarial impact on the Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) reserve attributable to this dispute. Populated by the actuarial team when the dispute outcome is uncertain and a reserve adjustment is warranted under GAAP or SAP.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944; NAIC Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP); LDTI (ASU 2018-12)

attributes.name: legal_counsel_assigned
attributes.description: Indicates whether internal or external legal counsel has been assigned to manage this dispute. Supports legal department workload tracking and compliance oversight.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; Internal Legal Operations Policy

attributes.name: life_insurance_position_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount that Life Insurance asserts is owed or correct per its own calculation or treaty interpretation. May differ from the disputed_amount if the position has been refined during negotiation.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; FASB ASC 944; SAP

attributes.name: open_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the dispute was formally opened and logged in the Reinsurance Management System. Serves as the principal business event date for aging and SLA tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: originating_transaction_ref
attributes.description: The source system transaction reference number (e.g., bordereaux period identifier, claim number, premium remittance reference) from the Reinsurance Management System that triggered the dispute. Provides an audit trail back to the originating transaction.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority assigned to the dispute, reflecting financial materiality, regulatory sensitivity, or counterparty relationship impact. Drives escalation and resolution timelines.
attributes.references: Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: rbc_credit_impact
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dispute has a potential impact on the Risk-Based Capital (RBC) credit claimed for the associated reinsurance arrangement. A True value triggers actuarial and finance review for RBC reporting purposes.
attributes.references: NAIC Risk-Based Capital (RBC) Model Act; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the required regulatory notification was submitted to the applicable state Department of Insurance or other governing body. Null if notification is not required or has not yet been submitted.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; State Department of Insurance Regulations

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dispute requires notification to a state Department of Insurance or other regulatory body (e.g., NAIC, SEC for variable products). Supports compliance oversight and regulatory reporting obligations.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; State Department of Insurance Regulations; SOX

attributes.name: reinsurer_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary contact person at the reinsurer counterparty responsible for managing this dispute on their side. Used for correspondence and negotiation coordination.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy

attributes.name: reinsurer_dispute_ref
attributes.description: The dispute or case reference number assigned by the reinsurer counterparty in their own system. Used for cross-referencing during negotiations and correspondence to ensure both parties are discussing the same dispute.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785

attributes.name: reinsurer_position_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount that the reinsurer counterparty asserts is owed or correct per its own calculation or treaty interpretation. Captured to quantify the gap between the two parties' positions.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; FASB ASC 944; SAP

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the dispute was formally resolved, withdrawn, or closed. Null if the dispute remains open. Used to calculate dispute duration and measure operational efficiency.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; ACORD Data Standards

attributes.name: resolution_method
attributes.description: The mechanism by which the dispute was resolved. Indicates whether resolution was achieved through direct negotiation, formal arbitration per treaty terms, mediation, litigation, or mutual agreement. Null if unresolved.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; AAA Arbitration Rules for Insurance Industry

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Narrative summary of how the dispute was resolved, including the rationale for the settled amount, any concessions made, and any treaty amendments or clarifications agreed upon. Populated at resolution.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy

attributes.name: settled_amount
attributes.description: The final monetary amount agreed upon at resolution of the dispute. Null if the dispute is unresolved. Used for financial reconciliation, recoverable tracking, and SAP/GAAP reporting.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; FASB ASC 944; SAP; GAAP

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational source system from which this dispute record originated (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS, RGA AURA Reinsurance). Supports data lineage and ETL audit in the Databricks silver layer.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: source_system_dispute_ref
attributes.description: The native dispute or case identifier from the originating Reinsurance Management System (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS case ID or RGA AURA dispute reference). Enables reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: ACORD Data Standards; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: target_resolution_date
attributes.description: The internally-set target date by which the dispute should be resolved, based on treaty settlement lag requirements, regulatory deadlines, or operational SLAs. Distinct from the actual resolution_date.
attributes.references: NAIC Reinsurance Model Regulation #785; Internal Reinsurance Operations Policy

products.name: reinsurer_credit_assumption
products.description: This association product represents the credit risk assumptions applied to each reinsurer for reserve credit calculations and RBC reporting. It captures the specific credit rating, collateral requirements, and RBC credit percentage that apply to a reinsurer under a given assumption set. Each record links one reinsurer to one assumption set with attributes that exist only in the context of this credit risk evaluation relationship. Used for NAIC Schedule S Part 6 reporting and statutory reserve credit calculations.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, a single reinsurer is evaluated under multiple assumption sets over time as credit ratings change, regulatory frameworks evolve (GAAP/SAP/IFRS), and valuation purposes differ (best estimate vs prudent estimate). Conversely, a single assumption set applies credit risk parameters to multiple reinsurers simultaneously for reserve credit calculations and RBC reporting. The business actively manages these credit assumptions as operational records for NAIC Schedule S Part 6 compliance and statutory reserve credit eligibility.

products.name: treaty_experience_analysis
products.description: This association product represents the analytical relationship between reinsurance treaties and actuarial experience studies. It captures treaty-specific experience metrics (A/E ratios, credibility weights, adjustment factors) derived from experience studies that analyze multiple treaties simultaneously or track a single treaty across multiple study periods. Each record links one treaty to one experience study with metrics that exist only in the context of this specific treaty-study combination.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, actuaries conduct experience studies that analyze multiple treaties simultaneously (e.g., all YRT treaties in a mortality study), and each treaty requires analysis across multiple experience studies over time (mortality, lapse, expense studies, plus periodic updates). The relationship captures treaty-specific metrics (A/E ratios, credibility weights, adjustment factors) that exist only in the context of a specific treaty-study combination and are used for experience refund calculations and treaty-specific assumption updates.

products.name: dispute_evidence
products.description: This association product represents the Evidence relationship between reinsurance_dispute and document. It captures the formal linkage of documentary evidence to reinsurance disputes, tracking the role each document plays in the dispute lifecycle (supporting evidence, correspondence, settlement agreement, legal brief), the direction of document flow (sent to reinsurer, received from reinsurer, internal analysis), submission timing, relevance assessment, and exhibit numbering for formal proceedings. Each record links one reinsurance_dispute to one document with attributes that exist only in the context of this evidentiary relationship.. Existence Justification: In reinsurance dispute operations, a single dispute routinely involves multiple documents serving different evidentiary roles (correspondence with reinsurer, treaty interpretation memos, actuarial analyses, bordereaux extracts, settlement agreements, legal briefs, arbitration filings). Conversely, a single document—particularly treaty interpretation memos or regulatory guidance—can be relevant to multiple disputes that hinge on the same contractual clause or regulatory interpretation. The business actively manages this relationship through a dispute evidence registry, tracking document role, submission timing, relevance scoring, and exhibit numbering for formal proceedings.

products.name: treaty
products.description: This association product represents the contractual relationship between a reinsurer and a product plan, capturing the reinsurer's authorization, capacity, and terms for accepting cessions on specific life insurance and annuity products. Each record links one reinsurer to one product plan with attributes that define the commercial terms, capacity limits, cession basis preferences, and competitive positioning that exist only in the context of this reinsurer-product relationship. This is the operational SSOT for reinsurance capacity management and treaty administration.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, reinsurers participate in multiple product plans based on their expertise, capacity, and risk appetite (e.g., Swiss Re may cover UL, VUL, and term products while RGA covers different products). Simultaneously, each product plan requires multiple reinsurers for capacity diversification, counterparty risk management, and competitive pricing (a $10M face amount UL product may be reinsured across Munich Re, Hannover Re, and RGA). The business actively manages these reinsurer-product relationships as treaty arrangements with product-specific capacity limits, cession terms, pricing competitiveness assessments, and authorization dates.

products.name: reinsurer_contact
products.description: This association product represents the operational contact assignment between reinsurance counterparties and their designated vendor contacts. It captures which specific contacts at vendor organizations (brokers, intermediaries, service providers) are authorized to represent or communicate on behalf of specific reinsurers. Each record links one reinsurer to one vendor contact with role-specific attributes that define the scope, authorization level, and temporal validity of the contact relationship.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, a single reinsurer (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re) has multiple designated contacts serving different functional roles (underwriter, claims manager, accounting, legal counsel) at vendor/broker organizations. Simultaneously, a single vendor contact (especially at reinsurance brokers or intermediaries) may represent multiple reinsurer clients. The business actively manages these contact assignments with role-specific authorization levels, treaty scope definitions, and temporal validity periods to ensure proper routing of treaty submissions, claims communications, and settlement instructions.
