domains.name: actuarial
domains.description: Owns all actuarial valuation, reserving, and experience study data. Manages GAAP/SAP/IFRS reserve calculations, PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20, cash flow projections, mortality and lapse assumption tables, DAC amortization schedules, LDTI transition adjustments, ALM analysis, and ORSA inputs. Supports Prophet/AXIS/MoSes model outputs, EOY/BOY reserve snapshots, pricing, product development, and ERM frameworks.

products.name: reserve_calculation
products.description: Core actuarial reserve calculation records capturing GAAP, SAP, and IFRS 17 reserve amounts computed per policy cohort or model segment. Stores net premium reserve (NPR), gross premium reserve (GPR), IBNR, PBR deterministic reserve (DR), stochastic reserve (SR), and LDTI liability for future policy benefits (LFPB). Includes point-in-time snapshot data: BOY and EOY reserve balances, net amount at risk (NAR), reserve per unit, and reserve change components (new business, terminations, interest accretion, assumption unlocking). Each record is linked to a parent valuation_run, assumption_set, cohort_definition, and pbr_model_segment. Sourced from Prophet/AXIS/MoSes valuation runs. Represents the primary output of the actuarial valuation cycle for statutory annual statement, GAAP financial close, and IFRS 17 reporting.

attributes.name: actual_events
attributes.description: Total number of observed events (deaths, lapses, disabilities, claims, surrenders) during the study period. Numerator for actual experience rate calculation.

attributes.name: ae_ratio
attributes.description: Actual-to-expected ratio calculated as actual_events divided by expected_events. A/E ratio of 1.00 indicates experience matches assumptions; >1.00 indicates worse-than-expected experience; <1.00 indicates better-than-expected experience. Primary output metric for experience studies.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the experience study was formally approved by the Chief Actuary or Actuarial Committee for use in assumption setting and valuation. Marks transition from draft to approved status.

attributes.name: assumption_locked_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) of whether the assumptions used in this study are locked for regulatory or contractual reasons and cannot be changed despite study results. True indicates assumptions are locked (e.g., PBR deterministic reserve locked assumptions); False indicates assumptions are open for update.

attributes.name: assumption_table_used
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the assumption table (mortality, lapse, disability, expense) applied to calculate expected events. Examples: '2017 CSO Preferred', '2008 VBT', 'Company Lapse Table v3.2', '2013 IAM Basic'.

attributes.name: assumption_update_cycle
attributes.description: Frequency at which this experience study is conducted and assumptions are reviewed for potential updates: annual (yearly), semi-annual (twice per year), quarterly, ad-hoc (event-driven), triennial (every three years).

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for actuarial commentary, observations, caveats, data quality notes, or special considerations related to this experience study. Used to document context that does not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: confidence_level_pct
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level (e.g., 90.00, 95.00, 99.00) used for credibility calculations and significance testing. Indicates the probability that the observed A/E ratio is not due to random variation.

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the actuary or analyst who created this experience study record. Audit trail for accountability and data lineage.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this experience study record was first created in the actuarial system. Audit trail for data lineage and governance.

attributes.name: credibility_standard
attributes.description: Qualitative classification of credibility level: full (credibility_weight >= 1.0, fully credible), partial (0.25 <= credibility_weight < 1.0, partially credible), limited (0.0 < credibility_weight < 0.25, limited credibility), none (credibility_weight = 0.0, not credible).

attributes.name: credibility_weight
attributes.description: Statistical credibility factor (0.0 to 1.0) assigned to this study based on exposure volume, variance, and confidence level per ASOP 25. Higher credibility indicates greater statistical reliability. Used to blend actual experience with industry tables when setting new assumptions.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the actuarial valuation or experience analysis system from which this study was generated (e.g., 'MoSes', 'AXIS', 'Prophet', 'Milliman Arius', 'Moody's ALFA'). Identifies the system of record for this experience study.

attributes.name: exclusion_criteria
attributes.description: Description of policies or data excluded from the study population (e.g., 'Policies in grace period', 'Reinsured policies', 'Policies with incomplete data', 'First-year policies'). Documents scope limitations and data quality filters.

attributes.name: expected_events
attributes.description: Total number of expected events based on current assumption tables applied to the study population exposure. Used as the benchmark for actual-to-expected (A/E) ratio calculation.

attributes.name: exposure_amount
attributes.description: Total exposure measure for the study population, typically expressed in policy-years, life-years, or face amount-years depending on the study type. Denominator for calculating experience rates.

attributes.name: impact_on_capital_amount
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact (in USD) on Risk-Based Capital (RBC) or economic capital if the recommended assumption adjustments are adopted. Used for capital planning and solvency assessment.

attributes.name: impact_on_reserves_amount
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact (in USD) on statutory or GAAP reserves if the recommended assumption adjustments are adopted. Positive values indicate reserve increases; negative values indicate reserve decreases. Used for materiality assessment and management decision-making.

attributes.name: materiality_threshold_met_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) of whether the experience study results exceed the company's materiality threshold for assumption changes. True indicates that the variance is material and requires formal assumption update; False indicates variance is within acceptable tolerance.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the actuary or analyst who last modified this experience study record. Audit trail for change tracking and accountability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this experience study record was last updated or modified. Audit trail for change tracking and version control.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next experience study review or update based on the assumption_update_cycle. Used for assumption governance tracking and planning.

attributes.name: peer_reviewer_name
attributes.description: Full name of the independent peer reviewer (typically a senior actuary or external consultant) who validated the study methodology and results. Required for material assumption changes.

attributes.name: policy_count
attributes.description: Total number of policies included in the experience study population during the observation period. Used for credibility assessment and statistical significance.

attributes.name: product_segment
attributes.description: Product line or segment scope for this study (e.g., 'Term Life', 'Whole Life (WL)', 'Universal Life (UL)', 'Indexed Universal Life (IUL)', 'Variable Universal Life (VUL)', 'Fixed Annuity', 'Fixed Indexed Annuity (FIA)', 'Disability Income (DI)'). May be aggregated or granular depending on study design.
attributes.references: NAIC Product Classification, SOA Product Taxonomy

attributes.name: publication_date
attributes.description: Date on which the experience study results and recommendations were published and distributed to stakeholders (pricing, valuation, risk management, senior management). Marks official release.

attributes.name: recommended_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Actuarially recommended multiplicative adjustment factor to apply to current assumptions based on study results. Calculated using credibility-weighted blend of A/E ratio and current assumptions. Factor of 1.05 means increase assumption rates by 5%; 0.95 means decrease by 5%.

attributes.name: recommended_assumption_change_pct
attributes.description: Percentage change recommended for assumption rates, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5.00 for +5%, -3.50 for -3.5%). Derived from recommended_adjustment_factor. Used for management reporting and assumption governance.

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory or accounting framework for which this experience study is conducted: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards), PBR (Principle-Based Reserving), VM-20 (Valuation Manual Section 20), LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements), or other. attributes.name: study_methodology
attributes.description: Description of the actuarial methodology and approach used for this experience study (e.g., 'Seriatim policy-level analysis', 'Aggregate cohort method', 'Duration-based segmentation', 'Attained age method'). Documents the technical approach for reproducibility and peer review.

attributes.name: study_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name or title of the experience study (e.g., '2023 Mortality Study - Term Life', 'Q4 Lapse Analysis - UL Products').

attributes.name: study_period_end_date
attributes.description: Ending date of the observation period for actual experience data included in this study. Defines the upper bound of the experience window.

attributes.name: study_period_start_date
attributes.description: Beginning date of the observation period for actual experience data included in this study. Defines the lower bound of the experience window.

attributes.name: study_status

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: ORSA stress testing and VM-20 stochastic reserves require independent scenario validation per model risk management. Validation_performed_by is text; FK enables validator independence verification, cr

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vendor. Business justification: Economic scenario generators are vendor products (Conning ESG, Moody's GEMS). Links scenario set to vendor for license tracking, model validation, vendor performance assessment, and regulatory complia

attributes.name: actuarial_system_source
attributes.description: The actuarial valuation system that consumed or generated this scenario for reserve calculations or cash flow projections (e.g., MoSes, AXIS, Prophet). Ensures traceability between scenario generation and reserve calculation systems. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MoSes|AXIS|Prophet|GGY AXIS|Milliman Integrate|FIS Sunrise|Other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: board_approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the board of directors approved this stress scenario analysis and capital adequacy conclusions. Required for ORSA regulatory filing and corporate governance documentation.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual Section 3, SOX Section 302

attributes.name: board_approval_status
attributes.description: Status of board of directors approval for this stress scenario and its conclusions. ORSA requires board oversight and approval of stress testing results and capital adequacy assessments. 'Pending' indicates awaiting board review. 'Approved' indicates board acceptance. 'Rejected' or 'Requires Revision' indicate the board has requested changes.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual Section 3, SOX Section 302

attributes.name: calibration_date
attributes.description: The date to which the scenario generator parameters were calibrated (typically the valuation date or a recent market observation date). Ensures scenarios reflect current market conditions.
attributes.references: NAIC VM-20 Section 7.E, American Academy of Actuaries ESG Guidance

attributes.name: capital_adequacy_conclusion
attributes.description: Management's conclusion regarding capital adequacy under this stress scenario. 'Adequate' indicates the company remains well-capitalized. 'Marginal' indicates the company approaches action levels. 'Inadequate' indicates the company falls below minimum thresholds. 'Requires Management Action' or 'Requires Capital Raise' indicate remediation is needed. Used in ORSA reporting to the board and regulators.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scenario record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404, NAIC Model Audit Rule

attributes.name: cte_level
attributes.description: The CTE confidence level for which this scenario is used in reserve calculations (e.g., 70.00 for CTE 70 per VM-20, 98.00 for CTE 98 for Variable Annuity reserves per VM-21). Represents the average of the worst X% of scenarios.
attributes.references: NAIC VM-20 Section 4.A, NAIC VM-21 Section 6

attributes.name: equity_return_path
attributes.description: Serialized representation of the equity index return path for this scenario across all projection periods. Typically stored as a comma-separated or JSON array of monthly or annual returns (e.g., 0.08,-0.02,0.12...). Used for Variable Universal Life (VUL), Variable Annuity (VA), and Fixed Indexed Annuity (FIA) crediting calculations.

attributes.name: interest_rate_path
attributes.description: Serialized representation of the interest rate path for this scenario across all projection periods. Typically stored as a comma-separated or JSON array of monthly or annual spot rates (e.g., 0.0325,0.0340,0.0355...). Used in discounting cash flows and crediting rates for universal life and annuity products.

attributes.name: orsa_filing_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) Filing Year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which this scenario was used in the ORSA filing (e.g., 2024). ORSA filings are required annually by NAIC for insurers meeting size thresholds. Links scenarios to specific regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: projection_period_months
attributes.description: The total number of months for which economic paths are projected in this scenario (e.g., 360 months for 30-year projection horizon). Defines the length of the cash flow projection period.

attributes.name: random_seed
attributes.description: The random number generator seed used to produce this scenario. Ensures reproducibility of scenario generation for audit and validation purposes. Critical for demonstrating compliance with VM-20 requirements that scenarios be reproducible.
attributes.references: NAIC VM-20 Section 7.E, American Academy of Actuaries ESG Guidance

attributes.name: rbc_ratio_under_stress
attributes.description: The company's Risk-Based Capital (RBC) ratio (Total Adjusted Capital / Authorized Control Level RBC) after applying this stress scenario. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 350.00 means 350% RBC ratio). Used to assess whether the company remains above regulatory action levels (200% Company Action Level, 150% Regulatory Action Level, 100% Authorized Control Level, 70% Mandatory Control Level) under stress.
attributes.references: NAIC Risk-Based Capital (RBC) for Life and Health Insurers, NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which scenarios and stress testing results were submitted to state insurance regulators as part of ORSA or other regulatory filings. Tracks compliance with annual ORSA filing deadlines.

attributes.name: scenario_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of this scenario, including any special characteristics, stress assumptions, or business context. Used for documentation and communication with management, board, and regulators.

attributes.name: scenario_generation_date
attributes.description: The date on which this scenario was generated by the economic scenario generator. Distinct from valuation_date (the as-of date for reserves) and calibration_date (the market data date). Used for audit trail and version control.

attributes.name: scenario_generator_version
attributes.description: Version number of the scenario generator software used (e.g., 8.1.2). Ensures traceability and reproducibility of scenario generation for regulatory audit.

attributes.name: scenario_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of this scenario within the scenario set (e.g., 1 to 10,000 for VM-20 stochastic reserve calculations). Used for ordering and referencing individual paths.

attributes.name: scenario_purpose
attributes.description: Business purpose for which this scenario was generated. Discriminates between Principle-Based Reserving (PBR) stochastic reserve calculations, Asset Liability Management (ALM) stress testing, Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) stress scenarios, hedging analysis for Fixed Indexed Annuity (FIA) and Indexed Universal Life (IUL) products, pricing, and product development.
attributes.references: NAIC VM-20, NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual

attributes.name: scenario_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this scenario. 'Draft' indicates initial generation. 'Validated' indicates actuarial review completed. 'Approved' indicates ready for use in reserve calculations. 'In Use' indicates actively used in current valuation. 'Archived' indicates retained for historical reference. 'Rejected' indicates failed validation and should not be used.

attributes.name: scenario_weight
attributes.description: Statistical weight assigned to this scenario for aggregation purposes. For equally weighted scenarios (e.g., NAIC 10,000 scenarios), this is typically 0.0001 (1/10,000). For importance sampling or stratified scenarios, weights may vary. Sum of all weights in a scenario set equals 1.0.

attributes.name: stress_severity
attributes.description: Severity level of the stress applied to this scenario. 'None' for baseline scenarios. Severity can be qualitative (Moderate, Severe, Extreme) or quantitative (1-in-X year event). Used in ORSA and Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) frameworks to assess capital adequacy under adverse conditions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: None|Moderate|Severe|Extreme|1-in-10|1-in-20|1-in-50|1-in-100|1-in-200 — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual Section 4, NAIC Risk-Based Capital (RBC) Framework

attributes.name: stress_type
attributes.description: Type of stress applied to this scenario for ORSA or ALM stress testing. 'None' indicates a baseline scenario. Stress types include mortality shock (increased death claims), lapse shock (mass surrenders or persistency changes), interest rate shock (parallel shift or twist), equity shock (market crash), pandemic (extreme mortality), credit spread shock, longevity shock (reduced mortality for annuities), expense shock, or combined multi-factor stress. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: None|Mortality Shock|Lapse Shock|Interest Rate Shock|Equity Shock|Pandemic|Credit Spread Shock|Longevity Shock|Expense Shock|Combined Stress — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual Section 4, NAIC VM-20 Section 9.C

attributes.name: stressed_reserve_impact_amount
attributes.description: The incremental reserve impact (in dollars) resulting from this stress scenario compared to the baseline scenario. Positive values indicate reserve increases; negative values indicate reserve decreases. Used in ORSA stress testing to quantify capital needs under adverse conditions.
attributes.references: NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual Section 5, ASC 944

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scenario record was last updated in the data platform. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404, NAIC Model Audit Rule

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: The date on which this scenario was validated by an actuary. Part of the actuarial control cycle ensuring scenarios meet quality standards before use in reserve calculations.

attributes.name: validation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting the validation process, any issues identified, adjustments made, or special considerations for this scenario. Supports actuarial documentation and regulatory audit requirements.

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The as-of date for which this scenario set was generated and will be applied in reserve calculations or stress testing. Typically End of Year (EOY) or Beginning of Year (BOY) for statutory reporting.

products.name: reserve_snapshot
products.description: Point-in-time reserve balance snapshots capturing BOY and EOY reserve positions by product, valuation basis, and reporting period. Includes DAC-related actuarial calculation inputs that feed into finance.dac_amortization for GAAP booking. This is the actuarial calculation output; finance.dac_amortization is the SSOT for the accounting entry.
products.reference: SAP Annual Statement Reserve; GAAP EOY Reserve Snapshot

attributes.name: reserve_snapshot_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the reserve snapshot record. Primary key.

Adding cohort_definition_id FK allows joining to the full cohor

attributes.name: in_force_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the policy for which reserves are being calculated and snapshotted.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.insured. Business justification: Reserve snapshots capture point-in-time reserve positions by individual insured life for regulatory reporting (statutory annual statements) and financial close. Insurers track reserves at insured-leve

attributes.name: valuation_run_id

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the reserve snapshot was reviewed and approved by the qualified actuary.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Requirements

attributes.name: av
attributes.description: The account value of the policy at the snapshot date. Represents the policyholder's accumulated value in universal life and variable products.

attributes.name: calculation_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the reserve calculation was executed by the actuarial valuation system.

attributes.name: csv
attributes.description: The cash surrender value available to the policyholder if the policy were surrendered at the snapshot date. Relevant for permanent life insurance and annuity products.

attributes.name: dac_balance
attributes.description: The unamortized deferred acquisition cost balance at the snapshot date. This actuarial calculation feeds into finance.dac_amortization for GAAP booking. This is the actuarial calculation output; finance.dac_amortization is the SSOT for the accounting entry.

attributes.name: expense_assumption
attributes.description: The per-policy or aggregate expense assumption used in the reserve calculation. May represent maintenance expenses, claim processing costs, or other operational expenses.
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: interest_rate_assumption
attributes.description: The discount rate or interest rate assumption used in the reserve calculation. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0350 for 3.50%).
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: lapse_rate_assumption
attributes.description: The assumed annual lapse or surrender rate used in the reserve calculation. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5.00%).
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: ldti_transition_adjustment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Transition Adjustment
attributes.description: The cumulative adjustment to reserves resulting from the adoption of LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements) under FASB ASC 944. Captures the impact of transitioning to updated GAAP reserve methodologies.

attributes.name: mortality_assumption_table
attributes.description: The mortality table used in the reserve calculation. Examples include 2017 CSO, 2001 VBT, or company-specific experience tables.
attributes.references: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20, SOA Mortality Tables

attributes.name: nar
attributes.description: The net amount at risk for the insurer, calculated as the death benefit minus the account value or reserve. Key metric for mortality risk exposure.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions, Actuarial Standards of Practice

attributes.name: net_reserve
attributes.description: The net reserve after reinsurance cessions. Calculated as reserve_balance minus reinsurance_ceded_reserve.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this reserve snapshot. May include explanations of unusual variances, assumption changes, or special considerations.

attributes.name: pbr_deterministic_reserve
attributes.description: The deterministic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.

attributes.name: pbr_net_premium_reserve
attributes.description: The net premium reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. Serves as a floor for the PBR reserve.

attributes.name: pbr_stochastic_reserve
attributes.description: The stochastic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20 using scenario modeling. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.

attributes.name: product_code
attributes.description: The insurance product code for which reserves are being held. Examples include WL (Whole Life), UL (Universal Life), IUL (Indexed Universal Life), VUL (Variable Universal Life), Term, SPIA (Single Premium Immediate Annuity), FIA (Fixed Indexed Annuity).
attributes.references: Internal Product Catalog, NAIC Product Classification

attributes.name: reinsurance_ceded_reserve
attributes.description: The portion of the reserve that has been ceded to reinsurers under reinsurance treaties. Reduces the net reserve liability for the ceding company.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Schedule S, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The reporting period this snapshot represents. BOY (Beginning of Year), EOY (End of Year), quarterly (Q1-Q4), or monthly. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BOY|EOY|Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|Monthly — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Quarterly and Annual Statement Filing Requirements

attributes.name: reserve_adequacy_status
attributes.description: The assessment of whether the reserve is adequate to cover expected future obligations. Adequate indicates sufficiency, Deficient indicates shortfall requiring premium deficiency reserve, Redundant indicates excess, Under Review indicates pending actuarial analysis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944, NAIC Annual Statement Instructions

attributes.name: reserve_balance
attributes.description: The total reserve amount held for this policy or cohort at the snapshot date. Represents the actuarial liability under the specified valuation basis.
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Schedule, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: reserve_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reserve being captured. Policy Reserve for contract liabilities, Claim Reserve for known claims, Premium Deficiency Reserve for loss recognition, IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) for estimated unreported claims, Unearned Premium Reserve for prepaid premiums, or Additional Reserve for supplemental reserves.
attributes.value_regex: Policy Reserve|Claim Reserve|Premium Deficiency Reserve|IBNR|Unearned Premium Reserve|Additional Reserve
attributes.references: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions, FASB ASC 944

attributes.name: snapshot_date
attributes.description: The valuation date for which this reserve snapshot was calculated. Typically BOY (Beginning of Year) or EOY (End of Year) reporting date.

attributes.name: valuation_basis
attributes.description: The accounting or regulatory basis under which the reserve was calculated. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards), PBR (Principle-Based Reserving per VM-20), or Tax basis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 944, NAIC SAP, IFRS 17, VM-20

products.name: pricing_basis
products.description: Master table defining actuarial pricing bases for life insurance and annuity products. Captures pricing mortality table, lapse assumption set, expense loading, investment return assumption, profit margin target (ROI/NBV), and regulatory compliance basis (GPT/CVAT for 7702). Links to product definitions and supports new product development, rate filings, and repricing reviews.
products.reference: Actuarial Pricing Basis; IRC 7702 Compliance Basis

attributes.name: pricing_basis_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the actuarial pricing basis record.

attributes.name: assumption_set_id

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the life insurance or annuity product for which this pricing basis applies.

attributes.name: plan_version_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.plan_version. Business justification: Pricing bases are version-specific; rate changes, assumption updates, or filing amendments require new plan versions per state insurance department requirements. Essential for tracking rate action his

attributes.name: policy_form_approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.policy_form_approval. Business justification: Policy form approvals require actuarial pricing basis for DOI review of rates, benefits, and reserves. Form and rate filings are often submitted together. Links pricing assumptions to approved policy

attributes.name: rate_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.rate_filing. Business justification: Rate filings submitted to DOI require actuarial pricing basis documentation (mortality tables, expense assumptions, profit margins). Pricing basis is the actuarial foundation for rate filing approval.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vendor. Business justification: Pricing models use vendor-provided actuarial software (Milliman Integrate, AXIS) or reinsurance pricing tools. Links pricing basis to vendor for license management, system dependency tracking, vendor

attributes.name: acquisition_expense_rate
attributes.description: Rate or percentage applied to cover first-year acquisition expenses including commissions, underwriting, and policy issuance costs. Expressed as percentage of premium or per-policy amount depending on loading method.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, GAAP ASC 944 DAC

attributes.name: age_basis
attributes.description: Method used to calculate insured age for pricing: ANB (Age Nearest Birthday), ALB (Age Last Birthday), actual (exact age in years and months).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pricing basis was formally approved by the appointed actuary or pricing committee.

attributes.name: approved_by_actuary_name
attributes.description: Name of the qualified actuary (FSA, MAAA) who approved this pricing basis for use.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Opinion Standards, ASOP No. 41

attributes.name: basis_code
attributes.description: Unique business code identifying this pricing basis configuration (e.g., STD_2024_UL, PREF_2023_WL).

attributes.name: basis_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the pricing basis (e.g., Standard Universal Life 2024, Preferred Whole Life 2023).

attributes.name: basis_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pricing basis purpose: new product launch, repricing of existing product, rate revision, competitive market adjustment, regulatory compliance update, or experience study adjustment.

attributes.name: competitive_position_target
attributes.description: Intended competitive positioning of rates under this pricing basis: market_leader (lowest rates), top_quartile, median (middle of market), competitive (within range), value (higher rates, richer benefits).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pricing basis record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: Rate used to discount future cash flows to present value for profit metric calculations (ROI, NBV). May differ from investment return assumption. Expressed as decimal.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this pricing basis becomes applicable for new business or repricing.

attributes.name: expense_loading_method
attributes.description: Method used to load expenses into premium rates: per_policy (flat amount per policy), percent_of_premium (percentage of premium), per_thousand_face_amount (per $1000 of coverage), tiered (varies by band), composite (combination of methods).

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this pricing basis is no longer valid for new business. Null indicates open-ended applicability.

attributes.name: filing_jurisdiction
attributes.description: State or jurisdiction code (2-letter abbreviation) where this pricing basis was filed for regulatory approval. May be multi-state or nationwide.

attributes.name: gender_distinct_pricing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pricing basis uses gender-distinct mortality and pricing (True) or unisex rates (False). Some jurisdictions prohibit gender-based pricing.
attributes.references: State Insurance Regulations, NAIC Model Laws

attributes.name: investment_return_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed annual investment return rate (net of investment expenses) used in pricing cash flow projections. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.0450 for 4.50%).
attributes.references: NAIC Asset Liability Management Standards, ORSA

attributes.name: maintenance_expense_rate
attributes.description: Rate or percentage applied to cover ongoing policy maintenance and administration expenses in renewal years. Expressed as percentage of premium or per-policy amount depending on loading method.

attributes.name: maximum_face_amount
attributes.description: Maximum death benefit or face amount (in currency) for which this pricing basis applies. Null indicates no upper limit.

attributes.name: maximum_issue_age
attributes.description: Maximum age (in years) at which a policy can be issued under this pricing basis.

attributes.name: minimum_face_amount
attributes.description: Minimum death benefit or face amount (in currency) for which this pricing basis applies.

attributes.name: minimum_issue_age
attributes.description: Minimum age (in years) at which a policy can be issued under this pricing basis.

attributes.name: mortality_improvement_scale
attributes.description: Mortality improvement projection scale applied to base mortality table (e.g., Scale G2, Scale AA, MP-2021). Used to adjust mortality rates for future improvements.
attributes.references: Society of Actuaries Mortality Improvement Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting special considerations, assumptions, limitations, or context for this pricing basis. Used for actuarial documentation and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: pricing_basis_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pricing basis: draft (in development), under_review (actuarial review), approved (ready for use), active (currently in use), superseded (replaced by newer basis), retired (no longer applicable).

attributes.name: pricing_model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the pricing model or software used to generate this basis. Supports model governance and reproducibility.

attributes.name: profit_margin_target_pct
attributes.description: Target profit margin as percentage of premium or present value of profits. Used to calibrate pricing to achieve desired profitability. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.0800 for 8.00%).

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_number
attributes.description: State insurance department filing number or SERFF tracking number associated with the rate filing for this pricing basis. Null if not filed or filed under product filing.

attributes.name: reinsurance_assumption
attributes.description: Type of reinsurance arrangement assumed in pricing: none (no reinsurance), YRT (Yearly Renewable Term), coinsurance, mod_co (modified coinsurance), facultative (case-by-case reinsurance).

attributes.name: reinsurance_cession_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of risk or premium ceded to reinsurers under the assumed reinsurance arrangement. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.9000 for 90% quota share). Null if no reinsurance.

attributes.name: reserve_basis
attributes.description: Accounting or regulatory basis for reserve calculations associated with this pricing: statutory (SAP), GAAP (US GAAP ASC 944), IFRS (IFRS 17), PBR per VM-20 (Principle-Based Reserving), or tax reserves.

attributes.name: smoker_status_pricing_flag

attributes.name: target_nbv

attributes.name: target_roi
attributes.description: Target return on investment metric used in pricing. Represents expected return on allocated capital. Expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.1200 for 12.00% ROI).

attributes.name: expected_contract_life_years

attributes.name: expense_assumption_rate
attributes.description: The assumed per-policy or per-unit expense rate for ongoing policy maintenance and administration, used in liability calculations. May be expressed as annual cost per policy or as percentage of premium.

attributes.name: geographic_market
attributes.description: The primary geographic market or jurisdiction where policies in this cohort were issued. Used for regulatory reporting, experience studies, and market segmentation analysis.

attributes.name: ifrs17_group_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Group Code
attributes.description: The IFRS 17 group of insurance contracts identifier. Groups are subsets of portfolios divided by issue year and profitability classification (onerous, profitable, neither).

attributes.name: ifrs17_initial_recognition_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Initial Recognition Date
attributes.description: The date when the group of insurance contracts was initially recognized under IFRS 17, establishing the cohort and locking in the initial CSM and discount rate.

attributes.name: ifrs17_portfolio_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standards 17 (IFRS 17) Portfolio Code
attributes.description: The IFRS 17 portfolio identifier to which this cohort belongs. Portfolios group insurance contracts subject to similar risks and managed together.

attributes.name: initial_csm_amount
attributes.description: The initial Contractual Service Margin calculated at initial recognition under IFRS 17. Represents the unearned profit that will be recognized as services are provided over the coverage period. Set to zero for onerous contracts.

attributes.name: initial_lfpb_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Liability for Future Policy Benefits (LFPB) Amount
attributes.description: The initial measurement of the Liability for Future Policy Benefits at cohort inception under LDTI. Represents the present value of expected future benefit payments less the present value of expected future net premiums, using the locked-in discount rate.

attributes.name: issue_quarter
attributes.description: The calendar quarter (1-4) within the issue year for more granular cohort segmentation when required by company policy or product characteristics.

attributes.name: issue_year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which policies or contracts in this cohort were issued. LDTI requires annual cohort grouping based on issue year to lock in discount rates and assumptions.

attributes.name: lapse_assumption_rate
attributes.description: The assumed annual lapse or surrender rate for policies in this cohort, used in cash flow projections and reserve calculations. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0350 for 3.50% annual lapse rate).

attributes.name: last_assumption_update_date
attributes.description: The date when actuarial assumptions for this cohort were last reviewed and updated. LDTI requires annual assumption updates at a minimum.

attributes.name: last_valuation_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which actuarial valuation was performed for this cohort. Used to track valuation currency and identify cohorts requiring remeasurement.

attributes.name: ldti_transition_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Long Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Transition Date
attributes.description: The effective date of LDTI adoption for this cohort, typically January 1, 2023 for calendar-year public companies. Used to determine transition adjustments and opening balances under the new standard.

attributes.name: locked_in_discount_rate
attributes.description: The discount rate locked in at cohort inception for LDTI liability for future policy benefits (LFPB) measurement. This rate remains constant for the cohort and is used to discount expected future cash flows. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0425 for 4.25%).

attributes.name: mortality_assumption_table
attributes.description: The mortality table used for reserve calculations and cash flow projections for this cohort (e.g., 2017 CSO, 2012 IAM, company-specific experience table). Critical for life insurance and annuity valuation.

attributes.name: next_valuation_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next actuarial valuation of this cohort, typically quarterly or annually depending on reporting requirements.

attributes.name: pbr_method
attributes.description: The Principle-Based Reserving methodology applied to this cohort under NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20 or VM-21: deterministic reserve, stochastic reserve, net premium reserve, or not applicable for products not subject to PBR.

attributes.name: policy_count
attributes.description: The current number of active policies or contracts included in this cohort. Used for coverage unit calculations and experience monitoring.

attributes.name: profitability_classification
attributes.description: IFRS 17 classification of the cohort at initial recognition: onerous (expected to be loss-making), profitable (expected to generate profit), or neither (break-even). Determines initial measurement and subsequent CSM (Contractual Service Margin) treatment.

attributes.name: reinsurance_treaty_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether policies in this cohort are subject to reinsurance treaties. True if reinsurance applies, False if the cohort is retained 100% by the direct writer.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date when this cohort definition was terminated or superseded, if applicable. Null for active cohorts.

attributes.name: total_account_value
attributes.description: The aggregate account value across all contracts in this cohort. Primary metric for annuity and universal life cohorts.

attributes.name: total_face_amount

products.name: alm_position
products.description: Transactional records capturing Asset Liability Management (ALM) position data including asset duration, liability duration, duration gap, convexity, and key rate duration profiles by product segment and reporting date. Supports interest rate risk management, hedging strategy decisions for FIA/IUL products, and ORSA internal model inputs.
products.reference: ALM Duration Gap Analysis; ORSA Interest Rate Risk

attributes.name: alm_position_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the ALM position record.

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: ALM positions require ALCO (Asset Liability Committee) approval by CIO/Treasurer for duration gap management and hedge strategy. Approved_by is text; FK enables authority validation, meeting attendanc

attributes.name: orsa_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.orsa_report. Business justification: ALM positions (duration gap, convexity) are disclosed in ORSA reports for interest rate risk assessment. ORSA requires market risk analysis including ALM. Links ALM measurement to ORSA filing.

attributes.name: portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.portfolio. Business justification: ALM (Asset-Liability Management) positions must reference specific investment portfolios to track duration matching and gap analysis. The alm_position product currently has product_segment_code/name a

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vendor. Business justification: ALM analytics use vendor platforms (BlackRock Aladdin, Bloomberg PORT). Links ALM calculation to vendor system for system dependency tracking, vendor risk assessment, contract management, and business

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of this ALM position record in the governance workflow.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this ALM position record was approved.

attributes.name: asset_convexity
attributes.description: Convexity measure of the asset portfolio, representing the curvature of the price-yield relationship. Used to assess second-order interest rate risk exposure.

attributes.name: asset_duration_years
attributes.description: Macaulay or modified duration of the asset portfolio backing this product segment, measured in years. Represents the weighted average time to receive cash flows from assets.

attributes.name: asset_market_value
attributes.description: Total market value of the asset portfolio backing this product segment as of the valuation date.

attributes.name: calculation_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this ALM position was calculated by the actuarial valuation system.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for actuarial or risk management commentary on this ALM position, including assumptions, limitations, or special considerations.

attributes.name: convexity_gap
attributes.description: The difference between asset convexity and liability convexity. Indicates the mismatch in second-order interest rate sensitivity between assets and liabilities.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this ALM position record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: duration_gap_years
attributes.description: The difference between asset duration and liability duration (asset_duration_years minus liability_duration_years). A positive gap indicates assets are longer-duration than liabilities; negative indicates the opposite. Critical for interest rate risk management.
attributes.references: NAIC Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_duration_years
attributes.description: Effective duration of the combined asset-liability position, accounting for embedded options and policyholder behavior assumptions. Used for hedging strategy decisions.

attributes.name: hedge_effectiveness_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage measure of how effectively the hedging strategy offsets changes in the fair value or cash flows of the hedged item, typically measured over the reporting period.

attributes.name: hedge_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of hedging instruments to the underlying exposure, indicating the proportion of interest rate risk that is hedged. A value of 1.0 indicates full hedge; 0.0 indicates no hedge.

attributes.name: interest_rate_scenario_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the interest rate scenario applied for this ALM position measurement (e.g., BASE for baseline, UP100 for +100 basis points, DOWN100 for -100 basis points, TWIST for yield curve twist).

attributes.name: key_rate_duration_10yr
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the portfolio value to a 1 basis point change in the 10-year key rate on the yield curve, holding all other rates constant.

attributes.name: key_rate_duration_1yr
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the portfolio value to a 1 basis point change in the 1-year key rate on the yield curve, holding all other rates constant.

attributes.name: key_rate_duration_20yr
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the portfolio value to a 1 basis point change in the 20-year key rate on the yield curve, holding all other rates constant.

attributes.name: key_rate_duration_30yr
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the portfolio value to a 1 basis point change in the 30-year key rate on the yield curve, holding all other rates constant.

attributes.name: key_rate_duration_5yr
attributes.description: Sensitivity of the portfolio value to a 1 basis point change in the 5-year key rate on the yield curve, holding all other rates constant.

attributes.name: liability_convexity
attributes.description: Convexity measure of the liability portfolio, representing the curvature of the liability value-yield relationship. Critical for FIA and IUL products with embedded options.

attributes.name: liability_duration_years
attributes.description: Macaulay or modified duration of the liability portfolio for this product segment, measured in years. Represents the weighted average time to pay cash flows to policyholders.

attributes.name: liability_market_value
attributes.description: Total market value of the liability portfolio for this product segment as of the valuation date, calculated using current discount rates.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the actuarial model (e.g., Prophet, AXIS, MoSes) used to generate this ALM position data, enabling traceability and reproducibility.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this ALM position record was last modified.

attributes.name: reporting_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary amounts in this ALM position are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: surplus_deficit_amount
attributes.description: The difference between asset market value and liability market value. A positive value indicates surplus; a negative value indicates deficit.

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the ALM position was measured and recorded, typically aligned with EOY (End of Year) or BOY (Beginning of Year) reporting cycles.

products.name: tax_qualification_test
products.description: Consolidated transactional records for all IRC tax qualification testing — IRC Section 7702 life insurance qualification (GPT/CVAT), IRC Section 7702A Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) testing, and related tax compliance calculations. Captures test type, test date, policy reference, test parameters, test result, and compliance status.

attributes.name: tax_qualification_test_id
attributes.description: Primary key for tax_qualification_test

attributes.name: annuity_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to annuity.annuity_contract. Business justification: GPT/CVAT tests determine if annuity contracts qualify as life insurance for tax purposes (IRC Section 7702). Required for MEC determination, tax compliance, and IRS audit defense. Currently policy_id

attributes.name: compliance_policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_policy. Business justification: GPT/CVAT testing enforces IRS Section 7702 compliance policy for life insurance tax qualification. Testing process implements compliance policy requirements. Links test execution to governing policy.

attributes.name: insured_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to policyholder.insured. Business justification: GPT and CVAT tax qualification tests require insured age at issue and attained age to calculate guideline premiums and corridor percentages per IRC Section 7702. Tests are performed per insured life,

attributes.name: mortality_table_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to actuarial.mortality_table. Business justification: Tax qualification testing (IRC 7702/7702A GPT/CVAT) uses a specific mortality table for calculating guideline premiums and cash value accumulation tests. The tax_qualification_test.mortality_table_cod

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: GPT and CVAT tests are product-specific; corridor factors, guideline premium limits, and seven-pay premium calculations vary by plan design. Required for IRC Section 7702 compliance testing and MEC st

attributes.name: test_performed_by_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Test Performed By Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GPT/CVAT testing requires qualified actuary or tax specialist for IRS compliance (IRC 7702/7702A). Test_performed_by is text; FK enables credential verification, authority validation, and IRS audit de

attributes.name: cash_value_amount
attributes.description: Cash surrender value of the policy at the time of the test. Used in CVAT calculations and MEC testing per IRC 7702 and 7702A.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Overall tax compliance status of the policy based on test results. Compliant = policy meets all IRC requirements, Non-Compliant = policy violates IRC rules, Remediated = non-compliance corrected through policy adjustment, Under Review = compliance determination pending actuarial or legal review.

attributes.name: corridor_percentage
attributes.description: Minimum death benefit to cash value ratio required under IRC 7702 to maintain life insurance tax qualification. Varies by insured age per IRC 7702(d)(2).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this tax qualification test record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: cvat_limit
attributes.description: Maximum cash value allowed under the Cash Value Accumulation Test per IRC 7702(b). Cash value must not exceed the net single premium for future benefits at any time.

attributes.name: death_benefit_amount
attributes.description: Face amount or death benefit of the policy at the time of the test. Critical input for GPT and CVAT calculations under IRC 7702.

attributes.name: guideline_level_premium
attributes.description: Level annual premium that would fund the policy death benefit over the insureds lifetime under IRC 7702(c)(4) assumptions. One component of the GPT limit calculation.

attributes.name: guideline_premium_limit
attributes.description: Maximum premium allowed under the Guideline Premium Test (GPT) per IRC 7702(c). Calculated as the greater of guideline single premium or guideline level premium.

attributes.name: guideline_single_premium
attributes.description: Single premium amount that would fund the policy death benefit under IRC 7702(c)(3) assumptions. One component of the GPT limit calculation.

attributes.name: insured_age_at_test
attributes.description: Age of the insured individual at the time of the tax qualification test. Used in mortality assumptions and guideline premium calculations per IRC 7702.

attributes.name: interest_rate_assumption
attributes.description: Interest rate used in tax qualification test calculations. IRC 7702 specifies rates between 4% and 6% depending on test type and policy characteristics.

attributes.name: mec_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the policy is classified as a Modified Endowment Contract under IRC 7702A. Non-MEC = policy passes seven-pay test, MEC = policy failed seven-pay test, MEC Pending = test in progress or under review.

attributes.name: net_single_premium
attributes.description: Single premium required to fund future benefits under IRC 7702(b) assumptions. Used as the CVAT limit for cash value accumulation.

attributes.name: next_test_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required tax qualification test. Used for periodic compliance monitoring and annual review scheduling.

attributes.name: override_approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized individual who approved the test result override. Required for compliance and audit purposes when override_indicator is True.

attributes.name: override_date
attributes.description: Date on which the test result override was approved and applied. Used for audit trail when override_indicator is True.

attributes.name: override_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the test result was manually overridden by an actuary or compliance officer. True = result overridden, False = system-calculated result stands.

attributes.name: override_reason
attributes.description: Business justification for overriding the system-calculated test result. Required when override_indicator is True. Documents actuarial judgment or regulatory interpretation.

attributes.name: policy_issue_date
attributes.description: Original issue date of the policy being tested. Used as baseline for IRC 7702A seven-pay test and other time-dependent calculations.

attributes.name: premium_paid_to_date
attributes.description: Cumulative premiums paid on the policy from issue date through the test date. Used in MEC seven-pay test calculations per IRC 7702A.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Description of corrective action taken to bring a non-compliant policy back into IRC 7702 or 7702A compliance. Examples include premium refund, death benefit increase, policy restructuring.

attributes.name: remediation_date
attributes.description: Date on which remediation action was completed to restore policy tax compliance. Used when compliance_status is Remediated.

attributes.name: seven_pay_premium_limit
attributes.description: Maximum cumulative premium allowed over the first seven policy years under IRC 7702A MEC test. Exceeding this limit causes the policy to become a Modified Endowment Contract.

attributes.name: test_calculation_method
attributes.description: Actuarial methodology used to perform the tax qualification test calculations. Must comply with IRC 7702 computational rules and assumptions.

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: Date on which the tax qualification test was performed. Represents the business event date for the test calculation.

attributes.name: test_notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes and comments regarding the tax qualification test. Used to document special circumstances, assumptions, or actuarial judgments.

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the tax qualification test. Human-readable reference number used for tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: test_reason
attributes.description: Business reason or trigger for performing the tax qualification test. New Business = initial policy issue, Policy Change = endorsement or modification, Annual Review = periodic compliance check, Premium Increase = additional premium paid, Benefit Increase = death benefit or cash value increase, Rider Addition = new rider attached, Regulatory Audit = external examination, System Migration = data conversion validation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_business|policy_change|annual_review|premium_increase|benefit_increase|rider_addition|regulatory_audit|system_migration — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: test_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the tax qualification test. Pass = policy meets IRC requirements, Fail = policy violates IRC limits, Conditional Pass = policy passes with conditions or adjustments, Not Applicable = test not required for this policy type or scenario.

attributes.name: test_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the tax qualification test. Pending = test scheduled but not started, In Progress = test calculation underway, Completed = test finished successfully, Failed = test execution error, Overridden = test result manually adjusted by actuarial or compliance.

attributes.name: test_system_source
attributes.description: Source system or platform that generated the tax qualification test results (e.g., Policy Administration System, Actuarial Valuation System, Prophet, AXIS, MoSes).

attributes.name: test_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the tax qualification test calculation was executed. Used for audit trail and sequencing of multiple tests on the same date.

attributes.name: test_type
attributes.description: Type of tax qualification test performed. GPT = Guideline Premium Test per IRC 7702(c), CVAT = Cash Value Accumulation Test per IRC 7702(b), MEC = Modified Endowment Contract test per IRC 7702A, 7702_COMPLIANCE = general IRC 7702 life insurance qualification, 7702A_COMPLIANCE = general IRC 7702A MEC testing.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this tax qualification test record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.description: The date when insurance coverage ends for this group of contracts. May be null for open-ended or lifetime coverage.

attributes.name: coverage_period_start_date

attributes.name: coverage_units_closing

attributes.name: coverage_units_opening
attributes.description: The quantity of coverage units at the beginning of the period used to allocate CSM release. Coverage units reflect the quantity of benefits and expected coverage duration.

attributes.name: coverage_units_provided
attributes.description: The quantity of coverage units provided during the reporting period, used to calculate CSM release.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this CSM record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: csm_accretion_amount
attributes.description: Interest accreted on the CSM balance during the period using discount rates locked in at initial recognition. Increases the CSM balance.

attributes.name: csm_assumption_change_adjustment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Contractual Service Margin (CSM) Assumption Change Adjustment
attributes.description: Adjustments to CSM for changes in estimates of future cash flows related to future service, excluding financial assumption changes and experience adjustments.

attributes.name: csm_closing_balance
attributes.description: The CSM balance at the end of the reporting period after all movements. Represents remaining unearned profit.

attributes.name: csm_experience_adjustment
attributes.description: Adjustments to CSM for differences between expected and actual cash flows related to future service. Does not include changes in financial assumptions.

attributes.name: csm_fx_adjustment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Contractual Service Margin (CSM) Foreign Exchange (FX) Adjustment
attributes.description: Foreign exchange translation adjustments applied to the CSM balance for contracts denominated in foreign currencies.

attributes.name: csm_initial_recognition_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Contractual Service Margin (CSM) Initial Recognition Amount
attributes.description: The CSM calculated at initial recognition, equal to the present value of future cash inflows minus outflows and risk adjustment, ensuring no gain at inception for non-onerous contracts.

attributes.name: csm_opening_balance
attributes.description: The CSM balance at the beginning of the reporting period. Represents unearned profit to be recognized over the coverage period.

attributes.name: csm_release_amount
attributes.description: The amount of CSM released to profit or loss during the period as insurance services are provided. Recognized as insurance revenue.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The functional currency for this group of contracts, expressed as ISO 4217 three-letter code (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: discount_rate_current
attributes.description: The current discount rate used for measuring fulfilment cash flows at the reporting date. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.04250 for 4.25%).

attributes.name: discount_rate_locked_in
attributes.description: The discount rate locked in at initial recognition for CSM accretion calculations. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.03500 for 3.5%).

attributes.name: fulfilment_cash_flows_pv
attributes.description: The present value of estimated future cash flows (premiums, claims, expenses) for this group of contracts at the reporting date.

attributes.name: initial_recognition_date
attributes.description: The date when the group of contracts was first recognized on the balance sheet under IFRS 17, typically the earliest of coverage start, first payment due, or contract becoming onerous.

attributes.name: loss_component_closing_balance
attributes.description: The loss component balance at the end of the reporting period. Zero for profitable contract groups.

attributes.name: loss_component_initial_recognition
attributes.description: The loss component established at initial recognition for onerous contracts, equal to the excess of fulfilment cash flows over premiums.

attributes.name: loss_component_opening_balance
attributes.description: The loss component balance at the beginning of the reporting period for onerous contract groups. Tracks expected losses separately from CSM.

attributes.name: loss_component_reversal
attributes.description: Reduction in the loss component during the period due to favorable changes in estimates or release as services are provided.

attributes.name: measurement_model

attributes.name: onerous_contract_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the group of contracts is onerous at initial recognition (expected to generate a loss). True if onerous, False if profitable or break-even.

attributes.name: product_line
attributes.description: The insurance product line for this group of contracts. products.name: orsa_stress_test

products.name: assumption_detail
products.description: Typed detail records under an assumption set capturing individual assumption values by assumption type (mortality, lapse, morbidity, expense, interest rate, credibility). Stores rate values by age, duration, gender, risk class, and other segmentation dimensions. Each row is typed (mortality qx, lapse rate, expense per-policy, credited rate, etc.) and linked to its parent assumption_set. Replaces the need for separate mortality_table, lapse_assumption, disability_assumption, expense_assumption, interest_rate_assumption, and credibility_factor products while preserving full granularity. Supports PBR credibility blending, experience study updates, and pricing model calibration.

attributes.description: The basis or philosophy underlying this assumption detail. Indicates whether the assumption is best-estimate, conservative, prescribed by regulation, based on company experience, industry table, or a blended approach.
attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements, ASC 944

attributes.name: assumption_detail_status

attributes.name: assumption_subtype

attributes.references: NAIC Actuarial Standards, VM-20 PBR Requirements

attributes.name: assumption_type
attributes.description: Type discriminator indicating the category of assumption this detail record represents. Determines which dimensional attributes are applicable and how the rate value should be interpreted.

attributes.name: assumption_version

attributes.name: data_source_reference

products.name: alm_strategy
products.description: This association product represents the operational Asset-Liability Management (ALM) strategy linking liability cohorts to investment portfolios. Each record captures the strategic pairing of a cohort_definition (representing insurance liabilities under LDTI/IFRS 17) to a portfolio (representing backing assets), including target duration matching, allocation weights, rebalancing rules, and effective dates. This is the core operational mechanism by which life insurers match liability cash flows to asset portfolios to manage interest rate risk, liquidity risk, and regulatory capital requirements.. Existence Justification: Life insurers operationally manage Asset-Liability Management (ALM) by strategically pairing liability cohorts (LDTI/IFRS 17 groups) to investment portfolios with matching duration and risk profiles. A single cohort is routinely backed by multiple portfolios for diversification across asset classes (e.g., fixed income, equity, alternatives), and a single portfolio commonly backs multiple cohorts for operational efficiency and scale. The ALM function actively creates, monitors, and rebalances these pairings with specific target durations, allocation weights, rebalancing thresholds, and effective dates.

attributes.name: cohort_definition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the liability cohort being backed by this ALM strategy

attributes.name: portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the investment portfolio backing this cohort under this ALM strategy

attributes.name: alm_strategy_type
attributes.description: The type of ALM strategy employed for this cohort-portfolio pairing: cash_flow_matching (match liability cash flows), duration_matching (match modified duration), immunization (match duration and convexity), dynamic_hedging (active derivative overlay), liability_driven_investment (LDI approach).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this ALM strategy pairing became effective. Supports historical tracking of ALM strategy changes over time.

attributes.name: investment_committee_approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the investment committee formally approved this ALM strategy pairing. Required for governance and audit trail.

attributes.name: last_rebalancing_date

attributes.name: rebalancing_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The maximum allowable percentage drift from the target allocation before rebalancing is triggered for this cohort-portfolio pairing. Specific to this ALM strategy.

attributes.name: strategy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this ALM strategy pairing: active (currently in force), pending_approval (awaiting investment committee approval), suspended (temporarily inactive), terminated (no longer in use).

attributes.name: target_allocation_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the cohort's liabilities that should be backed by this specific portfolio. Multiple portfolios may back a single cohort, with allocation percentages summing to 100%.

attributes.name: target_duration_years
attributes.description: The target modified duration in years for the portfolio to match the liability duration of the cohort. This is the core ALM matching metric to manage interest rate risk.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date on which this ALM strategy pairing was terminated or superseded. Null if currently active. Supports historical tracking.

products.name: assumption_application
products.description: This association product represents the application of actuarial assumption sets to specific product plans. It captures the effective period, regulatory basis, usage purpose, and approval status for each assumption set applied to each product plan. Each record links one assumption_set to one product_plan with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling assumption governance, regulatory compliance tracking, and product-specific assumption management across valuation, pricing, and illustration purposes.. Existence Justification: In life insurance actuarial operations, assumption sets are applied to multiple products across different purposes (pricing, valuation, illustration), and each product uses multiple assumption sets for different regulatory bases (GAAP, SAP, IFRS17) and business purposes. Actuaries actively manage these applications with product-specific effective dates, approval workflows, and override parameters. This is a core operational relationship in assumption governance.

products.name: assumption_data_source
products.description: This association product represents the data sourcing relationship between actuarial assumption sets and external vendor data providers. It captures the licensing, usage scope, and cost allocation for vendor-supplied data (mortality tables, lapse studies, expense benchmarks) incorporated into assumption sets. Each record links one assumption set to one vendor data source with attributes governing the terms of use, effective periods, and financial arrangements specific to that data usage relationship.. Existence Justification: In life insurance actuarial operations, assumption sets routinely incorporate data from multiple external vendors (SOA mortality tables, RGA lapse studies, LIMRA expense benchmarks, reinsurer assumptions), and each vendor's data products are used across multiple assumption sets for different product lines, valuation dates, and regulatory bases. The business actively manages these data sourcing relationships with specific license terms, usage restrictions, cost allocations, and version tracking that belong to neither the assumption set nor the vendor alone.

domains.name: investment
domains.description: Manages the general account and separate account investment portfolio supporting policy reserves and ALM objectives. Owns fixed income, equity, and alternative asset positions, trade execution records, FMV/NAV valuations, portfolio compliance monitoring (RBC, NAIC investment guidelines), performance attribution, CDR tracking, and investment income allocation. Supports ALM duration matching, variable product unit value calculations, and RBC investment risk charges.

products.name: portfolio
products.description: Master record for each investment portfolio managed within the general account or separate account. Tracks portfolio type (general account fixed income, separate account equity, alternative assets), ALM classification, investment mandate, benchmark index, risk tolerance tier, regulatory classification (NAIC Schedule D/E/BA), RBC charge category, inception date, portfolio manager assignment, strategic and tactical asset allocation targets, actual allocation weights, and rebalancing triggers. Serves as the SSOT for all portfolio-level investment positions, asset allocation governance, and performance attribution.
products.reference: NAIC Schedule D Portfolio / SimCorp Dimension Portfolio Master

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reporting.segment_definition.
